issues.title: Secret values never reach Terraform state: the SSM parameters use write-only values, not a placeholder with ignore_changes
issues.description_html:
As the owner I want no secret value ever stored in Terraform state, so that reading state (CI's plan role, the AWS MCP) can never reveal a key.

Found in the review of PR #32 (MA-155) and checked against the AWS provider. The rule in `.claude/rules/aws-changes.md` has Terraform create each secret's `aws_ssm_parameter` with a placeholder and `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }`, and Arun put the real value by hand. That leaks: the provider's Read fetches the parameter with decryption and stores `value` in state on every refresh (`internal/service/ssm/parameter.go`), and its docs say "The unencrypted value of a SecureString will be stored in the raw state as plain-text". `ignore_changes` only hides the diff. With the write-only argument `value_wo` (and `value_wo_version`; Terraform 1.11 or later), Read sets `value` to nothing, and "write-only values are never stored to state". No `infra/` exists yet, so this changes the pattern before anything is built.

**Where.** `.claude/rules/aws-changes.md` (the "Put a secret value" row), `TECH_STACK.md` (Secrets, Terraform), `README.md` (the `put-parameter` commands gain `--overwrite`, since Terraform creates the parameter first), `PLAN.md` phase 0, `docs/trace.json`.

**Acceptance.**

* The rule says: Terraform creates each secret's parameter with a write-only placeholder (`value_wo`, `value_wo_version`), never `value` or `insecure_value`; Arun overwrites it by hand; no secret is ever in state.
* Terraform 1.11 or later and an AWS provider with `value_wo` are pinned when `infra/` is written (MA-26).
* The README's commands put the value with `--overwrite`, read from the terminal (`read -rs`), never echoed.
* Gates: `python3 scripts/plan_sync.py selftest && python3 scripts/plan_sync.py check`.

**Depends on.** none. MA-26 (Terraform) builds to it.

issues.title: The app's shell, 1a Chat first: tabs on iPhone, the chat beside every screen from about 1133 pt, a sheet away from about 600 to 1133 pt, and a tab in a compact window (every iPhone, a folded foldable, Slide Over)
issues.description_html:
As a member I want one app that is the chat and the dashboard at once, on whichever Apple device I hold, so that I never hunt for where something is.

**The pick.** Arun picked **1a, Chat first**, on 26 Oct 2026 (with PR #36): the app opens to the chat, the household's total rides in a glass strip at the top, and pulling it down opens Home. 1b (Ask from anywhere) and 1c (One timeline) stay on `Shell options.dc.html` as the record, marked not picked.

**Where.** `ios/MyPaisa/App/` (the scene, `TabView` with `.sidebarAdaptable`, the inspector column), the boards `Shell options.dc.html` (1a) and `iPad and foldable.dc.html` in MyPaisa iOS v1.

**Boards to redraw.** This story's design-first round also redraws `Foldable · Open`, `Foldable · Open, Audit` and the caption of `Foldable · Folded` (on `iPad and foldable.dc.html`) to the width rule: at 880 pt, a tab bar at the top and the chat as a sheet (ARCHITECTURE.md 9.1). The two open boards draw the chat as a column beside the screen, and `Foldable · Folded`'s caption says three things the rule changes: that unfolding puts the sidebar and Home back beside the chat, that the chat column becomes the Chat tab, and that folding morphs the three columns back into the tab bar. Until then the rule wins over those boards.

**Acceptance.**

* Build 1a as drawn, nothing else: the chat is the first tab; the glass household strip at the top of the chat opens Home as a sheet when pulled down or tapped.
* iPhone (compact): the Liquid Glass tab bar with Chat · Home · Activity · You and the separate search tab; the tab bar minimises as content scrolls.
* **The width rule** (ARCHITECTURE.md 9.1): the window's width decides the layout, never the device, with one exception: an iPhone is always compact, its tab bar in portrait or landscape, as `iPhone · Landscape` draws it.

    * Under about 600 pt, and every iPhone (compact: an iPhone in portrait or landscape, Slide Over, one-third Split View, a folded foldable): the iPhone layout, the tab bar and one column, with the chat a tab.
    * About 600 to 900 pt (regular: an iPad in portrait, two-thirds Split View, an open foldable, a Stage Manager window): the sidebar collapses to a tab bar at the top, and the chat is a sheet over the screen, from its Ask or ⌘K.
    * About 900 to 1133 pt (regular: a 13-inch iPad upright, a wide Split View pane or Stage Manager window): the sidebar and the screen share the window, and the chat is a sheet away, from the sidebar's Chat, the screen's Ask or ⌘K.
    * From about 1133 pt (an iPad in landscape, a large Stage Manager window): the sidebar, the screen, and the chat beside every screen as a trailing column.
    * Widening past about 1133 pt turns the sheet into the trailing column, and narrowing below it turns the column back into the sheet, with matched geometry and no reload. Split View, Slide Over and Stage Manager windows from 320 pt wide lay out by width alone.
    
* A rotation, a fold or a window resize keeps the conversation, the scroll position and any guided flow (scene state restoration).
* Hardware keyboard: Return sends, Shift-Return breaks a line, ⌘K the composer, ⌘1 to ⌘5 the sections, ⌘F search, Esc closes a sheet; pointer hover on rows and buttons.
* Gates: the iOS gates (MA-166); snapshot tests of the shell at iPhone, iPad portrait and landscape, one-third Split View and the foldable sizes, light and dark.

**Depends on.** MA-165

issues.title: A merge to main sends MyPaisa Dev to TestFlight, and MyPaisa after Arun approves, with an alert before a build expires
issues.description_html:
As the owner I want app releases to go the way the Lambdas do, through CI and my approval, and stay privately installed on the household's iPhones and iPads across every 90-day (3-month) TestFlight window without ever appearing on the public App Store.

**Where.** `.github/workflows/release.yml` (with MA-107), `.github/workflows/testflight-keepalive.yml` (or Xcode Cloud inside the Developer Program's 25 free compute hours a month), `ios/ExportOptions-Internal.plist`, `ios/MyPaisa/Info.plist`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` 9.5, 15.2, 18.4, `docs/RESEARCH.md` 8.8.

**Acceptance.**

* Every TestFlight export sets `testFlightInternalTestingOnly = true` in `ExportOptions.plist` (so Apple's ingestion servers cryptographically forbid External Testing groups, public TestFlight links and public App Store submission, keeping both apps strictly private) and `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = false` in `Info.plist` (eliminating manual Export Compliance prompts so internal builds go live within minutes with zero Beta App Review), and verifies Release `com.mypaisapp.agent` strips all `#if DEBUG` Maestro hooks.
* Two separate Internal Testing groups in App Store Connect: `MyPaisa Dev` (`com.mypaisapp.agent.dev`, `Dev Dogfood` group, Arun only, side-by-side on the same iPhone and iPad) uploaded automatically from the `main`-only GitHub `dev` environment after `dev` smoke tests pass on a `main` merge touching `ios/`, and `MyPaisa` (`com.mypaisapp.agent`, `Household Beta` group: Arun plus invited family Apple IDs added under Users and Access with least-privilege `Customer Support` or `Marketing` role scoped strictly to `MyPaisa`, double-locked in-app by Cognito and single-use, 24-hour owner-created `/join/<token>` household invites) uploaded from the `main`-only GitHub `prod` environment only after Arun approves and prod's Lambdas pass read-only smoke tests.
* Every uploaded TestFlight build runs untethered on physical iPhones and iPads for a full 90 days (3 months), and TestFlight Automatic Updates install newer monotonic `CFBundleVersion` builds silently in place, resetting the 90-day clock to 90 days remaining while keeping Keychain tokens and MMKV offline cache intact.
* Evergreen 60-day renewal and phase-staged expiry safeguards: at day 60 of an active build's 90-day life, if no newer `ios/` build has shipped, a scheduled keepalive check (`testflight-keepalive.yml` / App Store Connect API `/v1/builds` age check, or Xcode Cloud free compute hours) publishes a day-60 alert (to `MA-231`'s `mypaisa-<env>-admin-alerts` SNS watch-tower topic in Phase 0, joining `ARCHITECTURE.md` 15.2's Admin center alert router once `MA-137` lands in Phase 8) and triggers a clean `CFBundleVersion` bump re-upload; on the client, compiled `MYPAISA_BUILD_EPOCH` in `Info.plist` drives a dismissible day-75 Warm Ledger build-expiry banner (`<= 15` days remaining) with a 1-tap `itms-beta://` action offline from Phase 0, joined in Phase 1 (`MA-266`) by FastAPI `GET /v1/app/minimum-version` for the hard minimum-version update prompt.
* Both UI states - (a) the dismissible day-75 Warm Ledger build-expiry banner (`itms-beta://`) and (b) the hard minimum-version update prompt - are drawn in MyPaisa iOS v1 with `/design-first` before the story starts.
* Gates: the workflow on a dry run; `ExportOptions.plist` `testFlightInternalTestingOnly` check and Release `#if DEBUG` strip check; the client `MYPAISA_BUILD_EPOCH` day-75 banner and minimum-version prompt logic unit-tested.

**Depends on.** MA-162, MA-164, MA-166, MA-107, MA-231 (and Phase 1 `MA-266` brings `GET /v1/app/minimum-version`; Phase 8 `MA-137` routes the day-60 alert through the Admin center).

Filed with MA-161 (the iOS app); expanded with private 90-day evergreen TestFlight beta mechanics and phase staging in MA-274 (29 Oct 2026).

issues.title: Every component, card and chart moves with one motion system, in the iOS app and the web app, and lands at once under Reduce Motion
issues.description_html:
As a member I want MyPaisa to feel alive and precise, with motion that explains what changed, so that the chat and the dashboard are a pleasure to use and never confusing.

Arun, 25 Oct 2026: "Make sure all the components and elements (including graphs and charts) have really good animation and motion effects all over the app (webapp and iOS)".

**Where.** `ios/Packages/MyPaisaUI/Motion/` (the springs, transitions and haptics as one module), every view; `web/` (the same choreography in CSS, the Web Animations API and View Transitions); the iOS kit's board `12 · Motion` in MyPaisa DS v1, and `motion.css` and `motion.js`, which every board in MyPaisa iOS v1 and MyPaisa app v1 links.

**Acceptance.**

* Content arrives with SwiftUI's `.smooth` spring (340 to 520 ms) and a 45 ms stagger, at most eight items; controls answer a touch with `.snappy` (a slight overshoot); only success moments (Saved, Face ID passed) use `.bouncy`; sheets use the system's curve. The glass bars never move with the content.
* The composer, the tab bar's lens, the segmented controls and the attachment menu morph through a `GlassEffectContainer` with `glassEffectID`.
* Every figure is a `contentTransition(.numericText())` with monospaced digits: it counts up once when it first appears, and afterwards only its changed digits roll.
* Charts (Swift Charts in the app, lightweight-charts on the web) draw in under a mask on first appear, dots and labels landing after; bars and meters grow from their base; scrubbing shows a glass lollipop with a selection haptic per point; a range change morphs the series.
* Messages push in from the bottom; streamed words fade in as they arrive; the typing mark runs only while waiting; a holding row zooms into its screen (`navigationTransition(.zoom)`); a red alert's mark pulses once; Confirm turns into its saved check with `symbolEffect(.bounce)`; the privacy eye uses `.replace`.
* Haptics: `.success` on Saved, `.warning` on a refusal, `.error` on a failed second check, `.selection` on chips, segments and scrubbing, a light impact on Send; none for passive updates.
* Nothing loops forever; transform and opacity only; 120 Hz on ProMotion with no dropped frames in Instruments on the heaviest screen (Home with its chart).
* Under Reduce Motion every movement becomes a 150 ms cross-fade or lands at once, figures land at their value, and haptics stay; on the web the same under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
* Gates: snapshot tests of each screen's final state, and UI tests with Reduce Motion on and off; on the web, Playwright with `prefers-reduced-motion` both ways.

**Depends on.** MA-165, MA-169

Filed with MA-161 (the iOS app).

**Stack (MA-229).** On the web the motion system runs on Motion 14 and Svelte transitions, with View Transitions; in the iOS shell Reanimated 4.7 moves only what the shell draws, and the SwiftUI pieces keep SwiftUI's springs.

An invite link opened in a browser shows MA-32's invite page (served by MA-73, not the login page), which says to open it on the iPhone; a browser never joins (ARCHITECTURE.md 4.5, "An unknown account" and "Joining").

issues.title: Re-plan: the household's whole wealth comes first, at every door, in clean renumbered phases
issues.description_html:
As the owner I want the plan, Jira, the trace and the docs to put the household's whole wealth first, with the agent, at every door, so that the build starts from one clean order and nothing drifts.

Arun, 26 Oct 2026: "I want to marry the wealth-tracker hosted on https://mypaisapp.com with the current development"; "For now just design and create JIRA stories and break into and clean phases, dont build anything".

**Decisions recorded (D1 to D12).**

* D1: the whole wealth comes first, in clean phases renumbered in build order (0 Foundations, 1 Talk, 2 The first record, 3 Deposits and two currencies, 4 Debts and check-ins, 5 Investments priced, 6 Budget, 7 Projection, 8 Audit and the Admin center, 9 The whole dashboard and the old tracker retired, 10 to 20 the market side as planned).
* D2: the web app is a full door with the chat.
* D3: SvelteKit 3 for the web app; SSE replaces the WebSocket live connection at both doors.
* D4: rule 4 rewritten: anything new is created in the chat; an existing figure can be corrected in place on any screen; one write service audits both.
* D5: a dynamic structure: kinds as data, records as documents, history as events, figures as views.
* D6: commitments and check-ins: the agent asks when something is due, and a tap records it.
* D7: the budget from statements and monthly check-ins.
* D8: Projection (the household's net worth over the years) is separate from Forecast (the market); plan items and saved assumptions are the admin's alone.
* D9: the iOS app is a React Native shell with a native SwiftUI core, as bong-panjika is built.
* D10: dashboard(-dev).mypaisapp.com replaces console(-dev); the live host goes.
* D11: both doors in every phase; a local stack, a seed and hydrated data.
* D12: the old tracker holds no real data; its screens and its tested maths are ported, not imported.

**Where.** `PLAN.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TECH_STACK.md`, `README.md`, `docs/trace.json`, `docs/TRACE.md`, `.claude/jira/taxonomy.md`, `.claude/skills/design-first/SKILL.md`, `docs/design/README.md`, `review/MA-161/fixed.json`; Jira epics and stories.

**Acceptance.**

* Six new phase epics; the fifteen existing epics renumbered; the new stories created and the existing ones rewritten, split or re-parented, each with its PLAN bullet and trace row.
* No record says the web app has no chat, no framework, console, later and not a priority, phase 8 done, read-only by construction, or an old phase number.
* Nothing is built: no code, Terraform, seed script or AWS change.
* Gates: `python3 scripts/plan_sync.py selftest && python3 scripts/plan_sync.py check && python3 scripts/contrast_check.py --selftest && python3 scripts/contrast_check.py`; `/plan-sync` shows no drift.

**Depends on.** none

issues.title: Phase 2: the first record is kept in one dynamic structure, registered through the chat or corrected in place, and the dashboard shows it live
issues.description_html:
**Goal.** The household's records live in one dynamic structure: kinds as data, records as documents, history as append-only events, figures as views rebuilt from them. The agent registers any kind through generic draft tools, asking only what is missing; one write service takes the chat's Confirm and an in-place correction of an existing figure alike, checks it against the kind and writes its audit row. The first kinds are the ones valued by the last figure given: savings, cash, a property's value and a pension's value. The first dashboard shows net worth and every record at every door, and moves live when a change is confirmed. PLAN.md phase 2; ARCHITECTURE.md 4.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/registry/` (kinds, records, events, views), the write service, the api's read routes and its correction route, `web/`, `ios/`.

**Done when.** You type "£5,000 in Monzo savings", choose whose it is, tap Confirm, and the net worth on the laptop moves while you watch on the phone; you then correct the figure in place on the dashboard and the audit log shows both changes, with who and when.

**Rules.** Anything new is created only in the chat; an existing figure may be corrected in place; both go through one write service with an audit row. Code computes every figure. Design-first for every screen and card, at both doors.

issues.title: Phase 3: deposits, savings, pensions and policies accrue to maturity, and every figure shows in pounds, rupees, dollars or euros
issues.description_html:
**Goal.** The kinds that accrue: UK savers and fixed-rate bonds, Indian fixed and recurring deposits, PPF, EPF, NPS, and policies such as LIC endowments, each valued by its own tested method, with a maturity timeline. ECB rates give every figure in GBP, INR, USD or EUR at the day's rate (Arun, 29 Oct 2026, MA-275: "The app should support 4 currencies"). A maturing deposit asks what happened to it, and a renewal starts its successor record. The old wealth tracker's tested maths is ported as golden fixtures. PLAN.md phase 3; ARCHITECTURE.md 4, 5.3, 6.6.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/registry/` kind specs, `wealth/` (accrual), `prices/` (ECB FX), `web/`, `ios/`.

**Done when.** You register an SBI fixed deposit and a UK fixed saver through the chat; their maturities show on the dashboard; the whole dashboard switches between pounds, rupees, dollars and euros; the accrual matches the fixtures to the penny.

**Rules.** Code computes every figure; contractual rates are used as given; design-first at both doors.

Updated 29 Oct 2026 (MA-275): two currencies become four (GBP, INR, USD, EUR); records are in the UK and India today, and one in the US or the euro area is added as data when it is needed.

issues.title: Phase 5: shares, ETFs, funds and mutual funds in the UK and India are priced every day with their XIRR
issues.description_html:
**Goal.** The market-priced holdings: OEICs, ETFs, shares, mutual funds, bonds and gold in UK and Indian accounts, registered through the chat as holdings inside their accounts, priced every day from free sources (yfinance for listed lines, AMFI's NAV file for Indian mutual funds) behind the PriceSource contract, with XIRR to the penny from the dated ledger. Where there is no history, the agent asks for past transactions or an estimate it marks as one. SIPs and regular contributions are commitments that record each buy. The Assets and one-asset screens show the value, the XIRR and its working. PLAN.md phase 5; ARCHITECTURE.md 4, 5, 6.6.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/registry/` kind specs, `prices/`, `wealth/` (XIRR), `web/`, `ios/`.

**Done when.** An ISA fund, an Indian mutual fund and a share are priced daily; each shows its XIRR, or the agent has asked for its history; the dashboard and the Assets screens show them at every door.

**Rules.** Free sources first; a failed or stale source is a normal day; code computes every figure; design-first at both doors.

issues.title: Phase 6: the budget plans each month and fills itself from statements and a monthly check-in
issues.description_html:
**Goal.** Each member's income, with its history so its growth can be measured, and a monthly plan per category, set through the chat. Bank and card statements sent in the chat are read, every line categorised, transfers recognised so nothing counts twice, and confirmed once; a payment on a statement answers its check-in. On the 1st the agent closes last month, asking only for what no statement covered. The Budget screen shows plan against actual, income, EMIs, surplus and the savings rate. PLAN.md phase 6; ARCHITECTURE.md 4, 12.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/registry/`, `importers/` (statements), the budget views, `web/`, `ios/`.

**Done when.** You send a month's bank and card statements; the agent shows one review card by category and you confirm it; on the 1st it closes the month; the Budget screen shows plan against actual at every door.

**Rules.** Every file sent is kept in S3 for good; card payments and transfers between your own accounts are not spending; design-first at both doors.

issues.title: Phase 7: the Projection shows where the household's net worth is heading, computed by code and driven by the agent
issues.description_html:
**Goal.** The Projection (the old tracker's Forecast, renamed; the market's forecasts keep the word Forecast): an engine that runs the household's net worth month by month to the horizon, from today's records, debts ending on their real dates, maturities, income growing at each member's own measured rate blended with the country's, spending inflating by country, each holding's XIRR shrunk toward a long-run prior, and the admin's plan items for future income and spends; deterministic first, then a Monte Carlo fan. The agent proposes the assumptions with their reasons, runs what-ifs and explains the curve; every figure comes from the engine. Since MA-261 (28 Oct 2026) the admin says what is coming (a new spend, a salary change, a loan closed) and is asked only what is missing; the engine puts out a budget forecast for each year to the horizon (20 years by default), and when a plan leaves the household short the agent proposes ways to rearrange the budget, applied on the admin's Confirm. PLAN.md phase 7; ARCHITECTURE.md 6.6, 12.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/wealth/projection.py`, the priors settings, plan items, `web/`, `ios/`.

**Done when.** The Projection screen shows the fan with its milestones at every door, opening at 20 years; a what-if in the chat shows a scenario without saving it; the admin says "GBP 4,000 a month from Jan 2029 for my kid's schooling", answers the agent's questions, confirms, and sees the Budget forecast and the fan move; a rearrangement applied on Confirm changes this month's budget; the admin corrects a plan item and an assumption in place; the engine matches its fixtures.

**Rules.** Claude never produces a number: a what-if's figures are traceable to the member's words or a named preset; plan items, rearrangements and saved assumptions are the admin's alone; every amount take-home, no tax maths; design-first at both doors.

issues.title: Phase 4: loans, mortgages, EMIs and cards are kept, and the agent checks in when a payment is due
issues.description_html:
**Goal.** Every debt is kept through the chat: home loans and mortgages, car and personal loans, EMIs and buy-now-pay-later, with dated terms, rate changes, prepayment by term or by EMI, and closure; credit cards as revolving debt from their statements. Commitments and check-ins make the agent ask when something is due ("was November's EMI paid?") and record the answer in one tap; "paid off in full" closes the loan. Autopay commitments and a weekly digest keep notifications to about ten a week. The Debts and one-loan screens show what is owed and when each loan ends. PLAN.md phase 4; ARCHITECTURE.md 4, 6.6, 8.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/registry/` kind specs, `wealth/` (schedules), the check-in job, `web/`, `ios/`.

**Done when.** You register a car loan through the chat; on its due date the agent asks whether the EMI was paid and one tap records it; "paid off in full" closes it and the dashboard and the debts screens move.

**Rules.** A check-in card shows exactly what a tap writes, so the tap is the Confirm, with Undo; a check-in is created once per due date; no LLM decides when to ask. Design-first at both doors.

issues.title: Design the whole-wealth screens at every door, with a clickable prototype Arun walks through before anything is built

issues.title: The web app's SvelteKit 3 PWA skeleton and the shared TypeScript models build, lint and test in CI
issues.description_html:
As the developer I want the web app's skeleton and the models both doors share, so that every later phase adds pages, not plumbing.

**Where.** `web/` (SvelteKit 3, Svelte 5, adapter-static, the PWA manifest and service worker), `web/src/lib/` (card types, formatting in GBP, INR, USD and EUR with lakh and crore, privacy masking, view models), `.github/workflows/`.

**Acceptance.**

* SvelteKit 3 with adapter-static builds a static app with a manifest and a service worker that caches the shell only; the fallback leaves `/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` alone; the CSP carries SvelteKit's hashes.
* The DS v1 tokens and the shared motion load; an empty shell renders at 390 and 1440 in light and dark.
* `web/src/lib/` holds the card types and the formatters, imported by path by the iOS app's React Native shell.
* Gates: svelte-check, eslint, vitest, Playwright 1.64 at `390x844` and `1440x900` in both `.t-light` and `.t-dark` through one shared `auditAndCapture()` fixture (`web/tests/helpers/audit-and-capture.ts`) running deterministic motion/font stabilization, fail-closed `@axe-core/playwright` 4.14 WCAG 2.2 Level A & AA before capture, keyboard focus/landmark checks (MA-181), and **Argos CI** (`@argos-ci/playwright`, Tokenless GitHub App OIDC, `uploadToArgos: !!process.env.CI`, `concurrency: cancel-in-progress`) capturing cloud visual PNG diffs in both themes (`threshold: 0.2`) and a light-theme-deduplicated YAML `ariaSnapshot` accessibility tree (\~3,600 snapshots/month inside the 5,000/month £0 Free Hobby tier, `docs/RESEARCH.md` §10), plus a pixel parity check against the boards and `pnpm audit`; verified in CI.

**Depends on.** MA-24, MA-25

Filed on MA-186 (26 Oct 2026), the whole-wealth re-plan.

* A one-off draws on `funded_from`; with none named, the surplus and cash in its currency first; a pool running short is a flag, never silent borrowing.

Arun, 26 Oct 2026: "Go with the latest and greatest for this. For UI, I want the what we used for Smart Clearance and bong-panjika, Tanstack, shadecdn-ui, tailwind CSS all those."

**The decision.**

* **The web app:** SvelteKit 3.1 and Svelte 5.57 on Vite 8.3, with TypeScript 6.0 (TypeScript 7 once svelte-check and typescript-eslint accept it), in a pnpm 12 workspace with one catalog of versions.

    * **Look:** Tailwind CSS 4.3, its theme mapped onto the Warm ledger tokens; shadcn-svelte 1.7 components on bits-ui 2.20, themed by the same tokens; Lucide icons (@lucide/svelte); Motion 14 with Svelte transitions for the shared motion system.
    * **Data and lists:** TanStack Query 6.3 for Svelte, TanStack Table 9.3 for the lists (assets, debts, statement lines, Audit, Activity), TanStack Virtual 3.13 for the chat and long lists, TanStack Form 1.33 for the in-place correction and the Admin center's settings. There are still no creation forms.
    * **Charts:** the dashboard's charts are shadcn-svelte charts on LayerChart 2.9; lightweight-charts 5.2 stays only for the market side's price charts.
    * **Tests:** Vitest 5 with Testing Library; Playwright 1.64 with axe-core; a pixel parity check of each screen against its board.
    
* **The iOS app:** React Native 0.88 with React 19.3, the New Architecture and Hermes, with no Expo, and TypeScript 6.0. Its parts:

    * native libraries: Reanimated 4.7 with Worklets 0.13, Gesture Handler 3.4, and MMKV 4.3 on Nitro Modules for the offline store;
    * data: TanStack Query 5.105 for React, sharing the query definitions in `web/src/lib/` with the web app on the same query core;
    * screens: every piece a member looks at is still SwiftUI on Liquid Glass. Tailwind and shadcn are the web's look; on iOS the look comes from the same tokens.
    
* **Swift Package Manager from day one:** React Native 0.88's `react-native spm`, opt-in and hardened in 0.88, before CocoaPods trunk goes read-only on 2 Dec 2026. A native library that cannot build with it is replaced. No CocoaPods.
* **The association file:** it is a static file at `web/static/.well-known/apple-app-site-association`, uploaded with `Content-Type: application/json`. A CloudFront Function sends extension-less page paths to the app shell and leaves `/.well-known/` and every real file alone. There is no S3 error-page fallback.
* **The stream:** API Gateway REST API response streaming (since Nov 2025, STREAM transfer mode, up to 15 minutes) on the api's own custom domain. It calls the `stream` Lambda: a Starlette app on Uvicorn behind the Lambda Web Adapter 1.1, with `AWS_LWA_INVOKE_MODE=response_stream`, its own target of the Dockerfile. MA-195 still measures the first delta, the resume and the cost; the route is no longer open.

**Where.** TECH_STACK.md §2 and §3, ARCHITECTURE.md §9.4, §9.5, §13, §16, §17, §21.5, PLAN.md (phase 0, phase 1, risks), README.md, docs/design/README.md, .claude/skills/design-first/SKILL.md, the trace, Confluence, and the descriptions of MA-165, MA-166, MA-194, MA-73, MA-195, MA-30, MA-199, MA-56, MA-58, MA-182 and MA-173.

issues.title: One trace follows a message from the door through the api, the queues and the agent to the model and back to every door, shared by every log line, span and RunRecord
issues.description_html:
As the operator I want one trace to follow a message from the door through the api, the updates queue, the agent, the model and the stores, the outbox and the sender to the stream and push, so that a slow or lost reply shows which hop it was at, and every log line, span and `RunRecord` of that message shares one id.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/obs/` (the tracer setup, the propagators, the resource attributes, the log formatter), the handler base in `handlers/`, `handlers/api` (the FastAPI correlation middleware and trace headers in and out, MA-266), the queue producers and consumers, `handlers/sender` and `handlers/stream` (the event envelope), `web/src/lib/obs/` and `ios/src/obs/` (the `traceparent` each door sends), the Dockerfile (the AWS Lambda Layer for OpenTelemetry unzipped into `/opt`), the smoke tests in `.github/workflows/`.

**Acceptance.**

* Both doors send a W3C `traceparent` on every call, new per action; the FastAPI `api` continues it through `CorrelationMiddleware` and `opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi` (recording the route template `http.route` for Application Signals), returns the trace id in `x-mypaisa-trace-id` and API Gateway's request id in `x-request-id` (MA-266), puts the message on `updates.fifo` with the trace header, and the agent, the sender and the FastAPI `stream` continue it: one trace in X-Ray and Transaction Search from `api` to the stream's delivery and the push, with the model, tool, DynamoDB, S3, SQS and APNs calls as spans.
* Every log line carries `trace_id`, `span_id`, `run_id`, `request_id` (on HTTP handlers), the member's hash, `client_message_id`, `conversation_id` or `job_id`, `env` and `build`; every span carries the same as attributes; the `RunRecord` carries `trace_id` and `build`; every `StreamEvent` and push payload envelope carries the `run_id` and `trace_id` of the run that made it, and nothing else about the trace.
* A scheduled job's trace starts at its tick and the work queue carries it; a replay by `scripts/redrive.sh` starts a new trace linked to the original by its `run_id`.
* Powertools Tracer is not used and the X-Ray SDK is not in the image; the OpenTelemetry SDK's cold-start cost on the `api` Lambda is measured and stays under 300 ms \[verify\], else the `api` keeps only the AWS SDK, FastAPI and HTTP instrumentations.
* The leak test: a recorded conversation with figures, names and a statement runs on the local stack with an in-memory exporter and a captured log, and no span attribute, span name, log line or metric holds a prompt, a reply, an amount, a name, a token or an account number; it runs in CI.
* The dev smoke test after each deploy sends one message and asserts, through the X-Ray API, one trace from `api` to `sender` within two minutes.
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest with moto and the leak test; verified on dev: one message's trace opened from its `run_id` in Transaction Search, with the stream's delivery and the push on it.

**Depends on.** MA-29, MA-31, MA-30, MA-139, MA-140, MA-231, MA-266.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/obs/llm.py` (the one wrapper every Anthropic call goes through), `src/mypaisa_agent/agent/` (the tool loop's tool spans), `runs.py` (the `RunRecord`'s model and tool calls), the metrics in the handler base, the model panel and its alarms in `infra/modules/mypaisa/observability.tf`.

**Acceptance.**

* One wrapper around `messages.create`, `messages.stream` and Batches sets, on a span named `chat <model>`, the OpenTelemetry GenAI attributes (`gen_ai.provider.name` `anthropic`, `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.response.model`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, the cache read and cache write token counts, `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons`, `gen_ai.request.max_tokens`) and MyPaisa's own (`mypaisa.cost_usd` from the price table, `mypaisa.feature`, `mypaisa.agent`, `mypaisa.step` of the ladder, `mypaisa.cache_hit`, `mypaisa.ttft_ms`, `mypaisa.refusal`, `mypaisa.fallback`), and never the prompt, the reply, a figure or a name; in dev only, a setting captures the prompt and the reply on the span for the synthetic household, and prod refuses the setting.
* Every tool call is a span `tool <name>` with its duration, outcome, error class and the sizes of its input and output; the `RunRecord` keeps the truncated input and output as `ARCHITECTURE.md` §10.1 says.
* The model metrics of §10.5 are emitted through Powertools Metrics: cost, tokens, cache reads, time to the first token, refusals, template fallbacks, tool errors and cancelled proposals, with the model, feature and tool in each metric line's own fields rather than as dimensions; the model panel shows them against the ceiling and the ladder's step; the alarms: a day's cost past the daily guard, refusals or fallbacks above 5% of calls in an hour, a tool's p95 over 10 s, no model call in a chat hour that had messages.

* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest with recorded `usage` blocks costed to the cent, and the leak test; verified on dev: one conversation's spans in the generative AI view with the right tokens and cost, and the model panel live.

**Depends on.** MA-29, MA-113, MA-232.

issues.title: The doors report what they saw, with the trace id and no content: the time to the first word, a resume or resync, an api error, a crash or a hang

issues.title: Container images are built on AWS CodeBuild's arm64 runner from GitHub Actions and stored in ECR by digest, inside the free tier
issues.description_html:
As the developer I want the Lambda images built on AWS itself, from the GitHub Actions workflow, and pushed straight to ECR, so that the arm64 images build natively (no emulation) on AWS's free build minutes and never leave the region.

Arun, 26 Oct 2026: "Can we do docker builds on AWS infra directly and store on ECR for free? If yes then that would be preferred."

**Where.**

* `infra/bootstrap/`, applied from the laptop only on Arun's ask (`.claude/rules/aws-changes.md`):

    * the CodeBuild runner project `mypaisa-ci-image` and its webhook;
    * its service role;
    * the `mypaisa` ECR repository and its lifecycle rule;
    * the usage budget.
    
* `.github/workflows/`: the image job.
* `Dockerfile`: its two targets, `lambda` and `stream`.

**What.**

* **The runner:** a CodeBuild project of the GitHub Actions runner type.

    * Its webhook filter is `WORKFLOW_JOB_QUEUED` for this repository only. Its source credential is the CodeConnections connection Arun makes once (MA-238).
    * Environment: `ARM_CONTAINER` on `BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL` (arm1.small, the free-tier type), the Amazon Linux aarch64 standard image, privileged mode for Docker, and the local Docker layer cache. No Docker image server: it has no free tier.
    
* **The job:** the workflow's image job runs on `codebuild-mypaisa-ci-image-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}`. Every other job stays on GitHub-hosted runners.

    * It builds both targets for linux/arm64 with BuildKit, using a cache mount for uv.
    * It pushes them to ECR tagged with the commit sha, and passes the image digests to the deploy jobs (MA-107).
    * The service role pushes to ECR, so no keys and no OIDC are needed for this job.
    
* **When it runs:** on every merge to `main`, and on a pull request only when `Dockerfile`, `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock` change (that build is not pushed). Runs of the same branch never overlap, and a newer push cancels the older run.
* **ECR:** one private repository, `mypaisa`, shared by dev and prod, so prod runs the digest dev tested. Scan on push. The lifecycle rule expires untagged images after one day and keeps the last five tagged images: prod's, its rollback, and dev's.
* **Staying free:**

    * CodeBuild gives 100 build minutes a month on arm1.small. That allowance never expires and covers existing accounts.
    * An AWS Budgets usage budget warns at 80 minutes. A cached build should take about five minutes, so about twenty a month are free.
    * ECR gives 500 MB free only in a new account's first year, then $0.10 per GB a month. The lifecycle rule keeps storage near 1 GB, about 10 cents a month.
    * Each image is kept small: a slim Python base, dependencies only, no build tools in the final stage.
    

**Past 100 minutes (Arun, 26 Oct 2026).** Builds go on past the free 100 minutes at about $0.0034 to $0.004 a minute on arm1.small, under a cent for a five-minute build. Arun: "lets keep AWS stack". So there is no fallback to GitHub's hosted runners for the image job; the 80-minute budget alert is a warning, not a switch.

**Acceptance.**

* A merge to `main` builds both images on CodeBuild in arm64 and pushes them to ECR by sha. The deploy jobs read the digests, and dev and prod run the same digest.
* A pull request that changes the Dockerfile or the lock builds the images without pushing them.
* The lifecycle rule, scan on push and the 80-minute budget alert exist in Terraform.
* A month's build minutes stay under 100 at the current pace. The first month is measured and reported.
* Gates: `terraform validate` and plan for `infra/bootstrap`, `actionlint` on the workflow, and the plan-sync gate.

**Depends on.** MA-26 (the bootstrap root), MA-238 (the GitHub connection). Feeds MA-107 (the release).

issues.title: Every board stays whole at every supported screen size and legible at 25% brightness
issues.description_html:
## What and why

Arun, 27 Oct 2026, asked for an independent UX review of every prototype and design, then for the glitches to be fixed: "The UI to glitch free, no overflowing or overlapping on different screen sizes", colour tones that hold at 25% mobile brightness, and "when resizing nothing should break or overflow". Then: "I want precise measurement and accurate pixel render".

Every current board in MyPaisa iOS v1, MyPaisa app v1 (the browser boards and Prototype v4) and MyPaisa DS v1 is rendered as Claude Design renders it, at the screen's own pixel ratio, in Chromium and WebKit, and every device and browser frame is resized through every size a member can have: an iPhone from 320 (Display Zoom) to 440 and in landscape, an iPad or foldable window from 600 to 1366, and the web from 320 to 1920. Prototype v4 is walked at every door, theme and step. Clipped text, text on text on the same surface, crushed columns, boxes cut at the edge, icons shown as their names, figures cut by an ellipsis and tracks that are not the token are faults. Every text, icon and chart mark was also measured against the real pixels behind it, at full brightness and at 25% (the model in scripts/contrast_check.py).

Main faults found:

* The web shell with the chat beside the page: the page's two columns followed the window, not the page, so at 1024 the page column collapsed to a word per line and at 1280 the hero figures collided.
* Rows that scroll sideways (the composer's shortcuts, the suggestions, the pins) were drawn as boxes that clip.
* The check-in card's four answers did not fit one row on an iPhone: "Paid off in full" was cut off at 402.
* Chart axis labels collided when the chart was narrower than drawn.
* Faults at 320, from 600 to 1133 and at 1024: filters, tables, detail cards, the file viewer, the Forecaster, the iPad's lists, iOS's alert, the inline title, the toast.
* The empty track and the projection's range band faded at 25%.

## Where

The shared stylesheet and motion script every board loads (MyPaisa DS v1 tokens.css and motion.js, copied into the iOS and app projects), the Foundations page, edited in Claude Design and copied into docs/design/. The gate is scripts/board_fit.js with scripts/board_fit_page.js and scripts/board_fit_allow.json; the record is docs/design/reviews/MA-240/decision.md.

## Acceptance

* At every size above, no text is clipped mid-word, no text sits on other text on the same surface, no column is crushed, and nothing is cut at the screen edge outside a row that scrolls.
* Every text, icon and data mark meets its tier at full brightness and at 25% (scripts/contrast_check.py's limits).
* At the drawn sizes nothing moves but the fixes review/MA-240/drawn-changes.json names, checked pixel by pixel against main.
* The fixes live in the design system, so the iOS app and the web app inherit them.

## Gates

* plan-sync gate (plan_sync.py selftest and check, contrast_check.py selftest and run).
* board-fit gate: node scripts/board_fit.js --selftest, then node scripts/board_fit.js (Chromium and WebKit), after npm ci --prefix scripts.
* The drawn-size pixel diff: node scripts/board_fit.js --diff d6e243f --expect review/MA-240/drawn-changes.json.
* python3 scripts/review_regress.py MA-240.

issues.title: Every holding, asset and debt shows a colourful icon for its kind, chosen from the kind's data
issues.description_html:
## What and why

Arun, 27 Oct 2026: "For different Holding type, asset type and debt type, can we dynamically have some colourful icons? Monzo app is so beautiful like that, I need something similar."

Today a record's row leads with a neutral monogram tile (VG, BA, FP). Each kind should instead show its own colourful icon, the same at both doors, so the household can tell a fixed deposit from a fund or a mortgage at a glance.

Dynamic, because kinds are data (ARCHITECTURE.md §4.8): the kind spec names the icon and its family, so a kind added as data gets its icon with no new code. A kind with no icon falls back to its family's tile with a monogram.

## The pick

Three options were drawn in Claude Design (MyPaisa DS v1, Kind icons: https://claude.ai/design/p/2f7310cd-e56a-4d13-8339-8fc637249c9a?file=Kind+icons.dc.html) and reviewed. Arun picked **B, Settings squircles** on 27 Oct 2026: "I want to go for option set B for icons" (A was recommended). B is the spec: a 36 pt rounded square with a gentle top-to-base gradient in a brighter version of each family's hue and a white glyph, one set for both themes. The record is docs/design/reviews/MA-241/decision.md.

## Before the build

Settled with Arun first (the trace row lists them as open, so the story cannot start): four glyphs that may mislead (personal loan, shares, PPF, gold and silver); NPS's family; whether account records (ISA, GIA, Demat, MF folio) get a tile; checking a kind's icon names when the agent proposes one after release. Drawn first (undrawn on the row): B's tile in the remaining states, a long holding name, many holdings with More, a stale price, loading, empty and error.

## Where

The design system (B's nine tiles and the white glyph as tokens in tokens.css, with their gate pairs), the iOS kit, the record rows on Home, Assets and debts and one record, at both doors. SF Symbols in the app; the boards draw them with Material Symbols. Its change to the colour tokens also settles two pairs MA-240's review left at the limit (Arun, 27 Oct 2026).

## Acceptance

* Options drawn in Claude Design through /design-first and B picked (done, 27 Oct 2026).
* Each family keeps its encoding's hue (shares blue, bonds violet, commodities grey, cash amber), in B's brighter tiles; green stays for gains only and red for alerts and destructive actions.
* Every glyph on its tile passes the ui tier at full brightness and at 25% (3:1 and 1.8:1, scripts/contrast_check.py's model), every tile is present on its card and page at the presence tier, and the gate measures the new tokens.
* The kind spec gains the icon and family fields (§4.8).
* The dark track on the success tint holds 1.25:1 at 25% with a margin (today 1.256:1 by the token values, and a pixel sample read 1.247): the dark success tint darkens a little, since a lighter track would take silver on it under 3:1.
* The light accent on the alert tint is a pair in scripts/contrast_check.py and passes 4.5:1 and 3:1 at 25% (today 4.49:1 and 2.97:1), or no board draws a link on that tint and the gate checks it.

## Gates

plan-sync gate; contrast_check.py with the new pairs; board-fit.

issues.title: The architecture records how the agents are guarded and evaluated: guardrails in code, evals gated on change, every live run checked, judges calibrated by the admin
issues.description_html:
As the developer I want the guardrails and the evals for every agent written down before phase 0 is built, so that each agent, tool, prompt and kind is guarded in code and tested on every change from the first run, and the suite grows with the agents instead of being rewritten.

Arun, 27 Oct 2026: "I want plan document and draft stories around Guardrails and evals strategy for the agents ... Deep research and propose the best solution for our agents which are highly dynamic, and will grow over time." His position: daily offline evals cost money, repeat the same score and breed alert fatigue; gate golden-set evals in CI/CD, monitor production online, and calibrate the LLM judges by hand on a schedule. His choices the same day: judges calibrated monthly and on every change; production transcripts stored only in our AWS account; Inspect AI is the harness. And on 28 Oct 2026, after review round 1: live evals in a Console workspace of their own, `mypaisa-evals`, at $10 a run and $30 a month on top of prod's and dev's ceilings; its key in SSM, read by a `ci-evals` role; each label and each new case behind the second check.

**Where.** `ARCHITECTURE.md` §23 (new: the rules, the guardrails, offline evals, online evals, calibration and growth, what runs on a timer, cost, the stories) and §4.1, §8, §9.3, §10.1, §10.4, §12.1, §13, §14, §15, §15.1, §15.2, §16, §18.4, §20.4, §20.7; `PLAN.md` (phases 0, 1, 2, 8, 11, 12 and 18, the risks, the definition of done); `TECH_STACK.md`; `README.md`; `docs/RESEARCH.md` §5 with its sources; `docs/trace.json`, `docs/roadmap.json`; a Confluence page of its own, Guardrails and evals (`scripts/confluence_docs.py`, with its fail-closed check); the descriptions of MA-21, MA-25, MA-37, MA-54, MA-68, MA-92, MA-104, MA-107, MA-113, MA-130, MA-132, MA-133, MA-197 and MA-198.

**Acceptance.**

* §23 records: guardrails strongest first (least agency, one policy gate in code before every call of our own tools, Anthropic's server tools only in a call with no household figure, untrusted text only as labelled data and a quarantined extractor, a conversation that has read such text losing its outbound tools, deterministic output checks, limits), mapped to the OWASP LLM and Agentic top tens; offline evals gated on change and never on a calendar (cases on the synthetic household, code graders first, binary judges only where code cannot measure; safety, regression and capability suites; T0 on every pull request; T1 when a prompt, a tool, a guard, the agent loop, the model routing, a kind template or the SDK changes; T2 on a model-id change, the release waiting for it before taking a new id to prod); online evals (code checks on every run, every flagged run and a random 10% judged overnight, alerts only when a rate leaves its band); the admin's calibration and the growth rules; and why §20.4's daily grading stays daily.
* The stack, decisions, cost and budget tables, the plan's phases, the definition of done, the trace, the roadmap and Confluence agree with it.
* The stories that build it exist with their rows, estimates and PLAN bullets (MA-246 to MA-256, MA-258).
* Gates: plan-sync selftest and check, contrast selftest and check; Confluence republished.

**Depends on.** MA-230, MA-228.

issues.title: One manifest declares every agent and tool, an Inspect AI harness runs tagged eval cases on the local stack, and CI refuses a tool, agent, prompt or kind template with no cases
issues.description_html:
As the developer I want every agent and tool declared once and every one of them covered by eval cases, so that a new tool, agent, prompt or kind cannot ship untested and the suite grows by adding tagged cases, never by rewriting (ARCHITECTURE §23.3, §23.5).

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/manifest.py` (the manifest), `evals/` (Inspect AI tasks, datasets, scorers and recordings), `scripts/eval_coverage.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

**Acceptance.**

* The manifest declares each agent (its model route and its tools) and each tool: its side effect (read, draft, commit through Confirm, external), the roles that may call it, its household scope, whether untrusted text removes it, its per-run limit and its eval tags. §8's Tools list is checked against it.
* Eval cases are Inspect AI datasets: a task on the synthetic household (MA-110's figure set), its graders (code on the outcome first, a binary judge only for what code cannot measure) and its tags (agent, tool, kind, flow, story key, and the suite: safety, regression or capability).
* T0 runs on every pull request with no network: the recorded conversations of MA-198 replay through the real agent loop and its guards, and the guards' own tests run.
* The coverage check fails CI for a tool, agent, prompt file or kind template with no safety case and no capability case; its selftest mutates a copy (a tool with no case, a prompt with no case) and expects each refusal.
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest with coverage, the coverage check and its selftest.

**Depends on.** MA-25, MA-110, MA-198, MA-245.

issues.title: Every tool call passes a policy gate in code: allowed for this agent and member, arguments in range, inside the household, within the run's limits, and narrowed once untrusted text is read
issues.description_html:
As the household I want every tool call checked by code before it runs, so that no prompt, file or web page can make the agent do what its manifest, the member's role or the run's limits do not allow (ARCHITECTURE §23.2).

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/guards/gate.py`, `src/mypaisa_agent/agent.py`, `evals/safety/`.

**Acceptance.**

* Before every call of one of our own tools the gate checks, in code: the tool is in the calling agent's manifest; the member's role and the household scope allow it (§4.5); the arguments match the strict schema and their ranges (an amount is the member's own text, parsed and typed by code, §4.7; only a typed override takes minor units and a currency code, §6.6); the run is under its tool-call cap and is not repeating the same call.
* Once untrusted text (a file's text, a fetched page, a news item) is in a conversation, that conversation, and every note and summary drawn from it, loses every tool whose side effect is external, so nothing holds private data, untrusted text and a way out at once.
* Anthropic's server tools (`web_search`, `web_fetch`) run inside one API request, where no code can stop a call, so they are given only to a call that holds no household figure (a holding's name and ISIN, never an amount), with `max_uses` set.
* The gate fails closed: an error or a timeout refuses the call. Each decision is an attribute on the tool's span and an entry in the `RunRecord`'s checks, where the overnight job counts the refusals (MA-252).
* Tests: each rule refuses a mutated call; a conversation that read a poisoned result has no outbound tool on its next run; the safety suite's injection and escalation cases pass all three trials.
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest with coverage, T0.

**Depends on.** MA-246, MA-29, MA-232.

issues.title: Every figure the chat states is checked against the tool results and the member's own words before it is sent
issues.description_html:
As the household I want every number in a chat reply to come from a tool result or from what I said, so that the chat never states a figure Claude made up, from the first phase it speaks (ARCHITECTURE §1, §23.2). The chat's half of MA-54's validator moves here from phase 11; MA-54 reuses it for briefs, wraps, alerts and cards.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/guards/figures.py`, `src/mypaisa_agent/agent.py`.

**Acceptance.**

* Every figure in a reply (an amount, a percentage, a count, a date) is matched against the conversation's tool results and the member's own words, after normalising the unit, the currency and the rounding (pounds and rupees, lakh and crore, thousands and millions).
* A figure with no match regenerates the reply once; a second miss sends the plain template. The result is an entry in the `RunRecord`'s checks.
* Tests: an invented figure, a figure in the wrong currency, a mis-scaled figure (a lakh read as a million) are caught; a correctly rounded figure, a figure the member typed and a figure from an earlier turn's tool result pass.
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest with coverage, T0.

**Depends on.** MA-246, MA-29.

issues.title: A trade, tax advice, another household's data or "sell everything" gets a plain refusal with the reason, and the red-team suite proves it
issues.description_html:

**Where.** `playbooks/` (the system prompt's scope), `src/mypaisa_agent/guards/`, `evals/safety/`.

**Acceptance.**

* A trade, tax advice, another household's data, another member's detail that is not shared with them, and "sell everything" each get a plain refusal with the reason and what MyPaisa can do instead.
* Code decides wherever it can (no tool exists for a trade; scope comes from §4.5); the prompt covers the rest.
* The safety suite asks each one directly, in several phrasings; every case passes all three trials. The same asks hidden in a file's text join with MA-253, and the stance card's "a view, not advice" line is the stance card's own (§9.2).
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest with coverage, T0, T1 on the prompt change.

**Depends on.** MA-246, MA-247.

issues.title: The chat's golden set, about 40 tasks on the synthetic household graded by code first, runs live three times on every pull request that changes a prompt, a tool, a guard, the agent loop, the model routing, a kind template or the SDK, within $10 a run
issues.description_html:
As the developer I want a change to anything the agent rests on tested against the real model before it merges, so that a regression is caught on the pull request, not in the household's chat, and no golden set runs on a timer (ARCHITECTURE §23.3).

**Where.** `evals/chat/`, `.github/workflows/evals.yml`, `scripts/eval_select.py`, `infra/bootstrap` (the `ci-evals` role).

**Acceptance.**

* About 40 tasks on the synthetic household. In phase 1: questions answered from the tools, asking one missing thing at a time, refusals, grounded figures. Registering, Confirm, cancel and correcting join with phase 2's draft tools and write service (MA-197, MA-201, MA-254). A case of several turns has the member's side scripted by slot.
* Graded by code first: the tools called and not called, the refusals, every figure grounded, and from phase 2 the `PendingAction` draft's values, the records after Confirm and nothing written before Confirm; binary judges only for "asked one thing at a time" and "plain and clear".
* T1 runs when a pull request changes a prompt, a tool, a guard, the agent loop, the model routing, a kind template or the SDK, and only the cases those paths cover; three trials a case.
* It runs in its own Console workspace, `mypaisa-evals` (Arun, 28 Oct 2026): $10 a run and $30 a month, the workspace's own limit the hard stop. A run that reaches its cap stops, is marked incomplete, never green, and the pull request waits for the admin's word.
* Its key sits at `/mypaisa-agent/dev/anthropic/evals_key` (MA-21) and only the `ci-evals` role reads it, for the evals job alone; the role is added to `infra/bootstrap` in an apply Arun asks for.
* Safety cases must pass all three trials; the regression suite must not fall below its baseline less its measured noise, with the standard error reported; a capability case that passes every trial in ten gated runs in a row graduates to regression.
* The result is posted on the pull request.
* Gates: the workflow's own test on a fixture pull request (the right cases chosen, a run stopped at its cap marked incomplete); T0.

**Depends on.** MA-246, MA-198, MA-21, MA-247, MA-248, MA-249.

issues.title: A model change waits for the full suite, five trials on the new model, before the release ships it
issues.description_html:
As the household I want a new Claude model proved on our own cases before it answers us, so that an upgrade cannot quietly change what the agent does (ARCHITECTURE §18.4, §23.3). Model ids are pinned snapshots, so a model changes only when we change its id.

**Where.** `.github/workflows/evals.yml`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `infra/dev`, `infra/prod` (the model ids).

**Acceptance.**

* A change to a model id, ours in `infra/dev` or `infra/prod` or a judge's, runs T2: the full suite, five trials a case, on the new id; the recordings are re-recorded. (A judge's prompt changing is a calibration trigger, ARCHITECTURE §23.5, not a T2 one.)
* T2 runs in the evals workspace, inside its $30 a month; a T2 that would pass what is left of it asks the admin first, with its estimate.
* The release workflow to prod waits for a green T2 on the ids it ships (MA-107); the result is in the pull request and the release notes.
* Gates: the workflow's own test on a fixture change; T0.

**Depends on.** MA-250, MA-25, MA-107.

issues.title: Every live run is checked by code, every flagged run and a random 10% are judged overnight, and only a rate that leaves its band raises an alert
issues.description_html:
As the operator I want every real conversation watched for the failures no test foresaw, without judging every run or ringing on every flag, so that live problems surface early and cheaply (ARCHITECTURE §10, §23.4).

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/evals/online.py`, `handlers/evals/` (the overnight job), `infra/modules/mypaisa/` (its schedule).

**Acceptance.**

* Every run records its code checks in the `RunRecord`: guard trips, the figure check, refusal, template fallback, tool errors, loop length and cost; and the member's signals: a question asked twice; from phase 2, a cancel after a proposal and a correction within 7 days of a Confirm on the same record.
* Overnight, every flagged run and a random 10% are judged by the same binary judges as T1, on Haiku through the Batches API, within 3% of prod's Claude ceiling, metered as the feature `evals` and pausing from the 85% step (MA-113); verdicts are `EvalResult` rows in the household's own table.
* Transcripts are stored only in our AWS account: the judges send them to the Anthropic API on the same terms as the chat, and no evaluation service stores them.
* The same job counts each rate (guard trips, figure misses, member signals, judge fails) and compares it, a week at a time and only once it has enough runs behind it, with its band over the last eight weeks. A rate outside its band raises an alert: until phase 8, a message on the owner's outbox and an alarm `RunRecord` (§10.6, MA-29); from phase 8, through the alert router (MA-137). The rest is listed in Activity (MA-196). No new CloudWatch metric.
* Judges stay advisory (listed in Activity, no alert) until the admin's calibration lands in phase 8 (MA-255).
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest with coverage, T0; the leak test stays green.

**Depends on.** MA-247, MA-248, MA-250, MA-113, MA-196, MA-231, MA-233.

issues.title: Uploaded files are read by a quarantined extractor with no tools, and poisoned statements and factsheets prove no instruction in a file reaches a tool
issues.description_html:
As the household I want what is written inside a file treated as data, never as an instruction, so that a statement, a factsheet or a sheet cannot make the agent write, fetch or reveal anything (ARCHITECTURE §4.6, §14, §23.2).

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/extract/`, `src/mypaisa_agent/agent.py`, `evals/safety/files/`.

**Acceptance.**

* `extract_document` runs as its own model call with no tools. A PDF or a screenshot goes in as a labelled document or image block; a sheet's or a statement's lines go in JSON-encoded and labelled with their source. Only the strict schema comes out, each field with its source line and confidence, checked by code (MA-37).
* Free text from a file reaches the chat only as labelled data, never as an instruction; a conversation that has read it loses its outbound tools (MA-247).
* A red-team set of poisoned files (a statement, a factsheet, a screenshot, a merchant name) tells the agent to write, to fetch a link, to reveal another member's figures, to trade or to give tax advice (MA-249's asks, hidden in a file); none reaches a tool or a reply, in every one of three trials. Each later importer (CAS, Excel) adds its own poisoned cases.
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest with coverage, T0, T1 on the extractor's prompt.

**Depends on.** MA-247, MA-249, MA-37.

issues.title: Each kind's field spec generates its own draft cases, so a new kind or field is tested before the admin approves it
issues.description_html:
As the admin I want a new kind of holding tested before it is approved, so that the dynamic structure can grow without anyone writing its tests by hand (ARCHITECTURE §4.8, §23.5).

**Where.** `evals/kinds/`, `src/mypaisa_agent/registry/` (the kind templates).

**Acceptance.**

* Each kind template's field spec generates draft cases: varied phrasings, both currencies, dates in several forms, a missing field; graded by code on the draft's parsed values and on what the agent asks for.
* Approving a new kind or field (`propose_kind`, behind the second check) runs its generated cases first in the evals job, on the seed household, and the approval card shows the result before Confirm (drawn with MA-197's boards, in its undrawn list).
* Every kind so far has its generated cases in the regression suite, and each later kind gets them through the coverage check (MA-246).
* The golden set's registering, Confirm, cancel and correcting cases (MA-250) join here, graded on the draft and the records it leaves.
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest with coverage, T0.

**Depends on.** MA-246, MA-250, MA-27, MA-197, MA-201.

issues.title: The admin labels a monthly sample of runs in the Admin center, each judge's agreement is measured, a drifting judge drops to advisory, and a failed run becomes a regression case
issues.description_html:
As the admin I want to check the judges against my own reading of real runs once a month and whenever something changes, so that their verdicts can be trusted and a real failure becomes a permanent test (ARCHITECTURE §9.3, §23.4, §23.5). Arun, 27 Oct 2026: monthly and on every change; 28 Oct 2026: each label and each new case behind the second check.

**Where.** the Admin center's Evals page at both doors (`ios/`, `web/`), `src/mypaisa_agent/evals/calibrate.py`, `handlers/api`, the `EvalLabel` item.

**Acceptance.**

* Each month the Evals page offers about 30 runs: every run where a judge and a code check disagree, the flagged runs and a random share, each with its transcript, tool calls and verdicts. A session also opens when a judge, prompt, tool or model changes and when flags spike.
* The admin marks pass or fail for each failure mode with a one-line critique; each label is behind the second check (§4.5) and writes an audit row.
* Labels accumulate: each `EvalLabel` keeps the transcript of the run it labels past that run's ninety days, so a changed judge is measured again on the same runs.
* A judge acts only once it has at least 50 pass and 50 fail labels it was not built from; until then, and whenever its true-positive or true-negative rate falls below 0.8, it is advisory until a pull request fixes it.
* A run the admin marks as failed becomes a regression case once it is rewritten onto the synthetic household and the admin confirms it, behind the second check; nothing of the household's own leaves the account.
* The eval caps (prod's judges at 3%; the evals workspace's $10 a run) are shown and moved here, behind the second check (§23.7).
* The boards are drawn with `/design-first` before the story starts.
* Gates: the web and iOS gates for the screens, pytest with coverage, T0.

**Depends on.** MA-252, MA-116, MA-184, MA-76.

issues.title: Each team agent has its own tools and safety suite, and a change it proposes to a prompt, rule or model carries its eval results to the admin's approval
issues.description_html:
As the admin I want each agent on the team limited to its own tools and every change it proposes tested before I approve it, so that a self-learning team cannot widen its reach or ship an untested rule (ARCHITECTURE §20.2, §20.3, §23.5).

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/manifest.py`, `agents/`, `evals/team/`, the admin desk.

**Acceptance.**

* Each team agent (data steward, news scout, analyst, Forecaster, grader and tuner, ops warden, budget keeper, admin desk) has its manifest entry (tools, model route, limits) and its safety suite.
* The agents talk only through the event bus and the settings service, every message typed and checked like a tool call; no agent takes another's text as an instruction.
* A `ChangeRequest` that changes a prompt, a rule, a threshold or a model carries the affected suites' T1 results; the approval shows them and a failing safety case blocks it (drawn with MA-130's boards, in its undrawn list).
* A proposal drawn from uploaded or fetched text says so, and where it came from.
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest with coverage, T0.

**Depends on.** MA-246, MA-250, MA-129, MA-130.

issues.title: The whole architecture and every journey recorded in Confluence, page by page, colourful and animated
issues.description_html:
As the admin I want a full, colourful record of MyPaisa's architecture and every journey in Confluence, with the animations from the explainer pages, so that everything we designed can be read in one place without opening the repo.

I need full record of everything, Do this in a parallel task and upload to confluence, no need of extra review".

**Where.** scripts/confluence_docs.py (the record pages, their text drawn from ARCHITECTURE.md and the explainer pages), a capture script for the animations, docs/confluence/record-\*.html, docs/confluence.json; space mypaisaa-agent under the hub.

* Animated GIFs captured from the explainer pages are attached and shown; the four Claude artifacts are linked as cards; the Lucid drawings and their generator are recorded.

No independent review, by Arun's word.

issues.title: The guardrails and evals are explained on a page of their own with animated diagrams, synced to Confluence, and the other explainer pages show them too
issues.description_html:

Arun, 28 Oct 2026: "make sure we create a detailed architecture diagrams in animated gif from and a html claude artifact to explain the evals and judjes and evrything in technical and simple terms. Sync them to confluence too." Filed first from review round 1 of MA-245 (lesson 5: an owner decision changes every record at once).

issues.title: The Claude Design boards and the repo mirror stay the same: one command pulls every change, a check fails on any drift, and a plan for Claude Design's move into Claude
issues.description_html:
As the developer I want one command in Claude Code that pulls every changed Claude Design file into docs/design/ and records its etag, and a check that fails whenever Claude Design and the mirror differ, so that the boards and the repo never drift; and a plan, picked by Arun, for when standalone Claude Design closes (by 14 Dec 2026) and moves into Claude as the Design Artifact type.

**Where.** scripts/design_sync.py (new), scripts/plan_sync.py (selftest), docs/design/claude-design.json, docs/design/ios-v1/, ds-v1/, app-v1/, .claude/skills/plan-sync/, .claude/skills/design-first/, .claude/rules/plan-sync.md, .claude/hooks/plan_sync_hook.py, .claude/jira-flow.json, docs/design/README.md, PLAN.md, docs/trace.json, docs/roadmap.json, Confluence phase 0.

**Acceptance.**

* A drift report on 28 Oct 2026: every file added, removed or changed on either side across MyPaisa iOS v1, MyPaisa DS v1 and MyPaisa app v1 against docs/design/claude-design.json.
* `python3 scripts/design_sync.py pull` lists the three projects, copies every new or changed file byte for byte (decoded, its size checked against Claude Design's listing), records etag, bytes and sha256, and reports files gone from Claude Design without deleting them. `python3 scripts/design_sync.py check` exits non-zero on any difference, fails closed when Claude Design cannot be read, and runs before every PR.

* The mirror matches Claude Design.
* The shutdown options (move the boards to Design Artifacts, make the repo mirror the only record, or another) with costs and a recommendation, and every place that assumes the old projects or URLs listed. Arun picks; nothing is migrated before he does.
* Gates: plan-sync (selftest, check, contrast), board-fit, design_sync check; verified on a live pull of the three projects.

issues.title: Designs are drawn in the repo and shown as Claude Artifacts; nothing is written to Claude Design, and its sync, gate and hook keep only their repo half
issues.description_html:
**Decided** (Arun, 30 Oct 2026): "for all future design use Local folder and then Claude Artifact. Claude Design is going away, so no need to push to claude design". MA-259's option B, now, in place of 28 Oct's "Wait for Move" (docs/design/reviews/MA-259/decision.md, The pick, changed).

Scripts and gates: scripts/design_sync.py (record, check, published; the connector and pull removed), scripts/plan_sync.py, .claude/hooks/plan_sync_hook.py, .claude/jira-flow.json, .github/workflows/plan-sync.yml, board_fit, contrast_check, the review ledgers, docs/design/claude-design.json (the repo's record now; its name is history), docs/design/boards-artifact.json (new). Rules and skills: .claude/rules/plan-sync.md rule 7 and its tables, independent-review lesson 9, the taxonomy, design-first, plan-sync, autoship. Docs and links: README, docs/design/README.md, ARCHITECTURE, TECH_STACK, PLAN, RESEARCH, the explainer pages, the Confluence generator's links, scripts/boards_page/ (builds the MyPaisa Boards Artifact, https://claude.ai/artifact/G6Dzu3QYtNPVkqyH4q9d6g).

issues.title: The plan records future plans by talking: new spends, salary changes and loan closures, a 20-year budget forecast, and the budget rearranged on the admin's Confirm
issues.description_html:
As the owner I want to say what I expect to happen ("GBP 4,000 a month from Jan 2029 for my kid's schooling", "my salary goes to GBP 8,000 a month from Sep 2028", "INR 2 cr to close my SBI home loan"), be asked only what is missing, and see the budget and the Projection recalculated for the years ahead, so that the plan shows what is coming, not only today.

**Where.** Docs only: PLAN.md phases 6 and 7, ARCHITECTURE.md 2, 4.1, 4.5, 4.10, 6.6, 8, 9.3 and 12, the trace, the roadmap, the explainer pages and the Confluence pages generated from them.

**Arun's decisions, 28 Oct 2026.**

* Plans stay the admin's alone (MA-222): members view the Projection and ask what-ifs, saving nothing.
* Rearranging: the agent proposes options, as Claude proposes changes; on the admin's Confirm the chosen option is applied, the current month's budget plan included, with an audit row and Undo.
* No tax calculation: every amount is take-home.
* A one-off with no source named is paid from the surplus and cash first.
* The Projection opens at 20 years, with 5, 10, 20 and 30 to choose; the engine's default horizon is 20 years.

**Acceptance.**

* A plan item has one of three effects: a new flow, a change to an existing flow (a salary, a SIP, a budget category) from a date, or an event on a record (a loan prepaid or closed, freeing its EMI).
* The agent asks only for what is missing, at most three questions with chips; every number traces to the admin's words, a named prior or the engine.
* The engine adds a budget forecast ledger (per month and per year) and a trace for every figure; money in Decimal.
* A shortfall gets options computed by code; the admin's Confirm applies one.
* Every plan, correction, pause and rearrangement is audited with the admin's own words and the Projection run before and after.
* The plan, the architecture, the trace, the roadmap and Confluence agree; the new screens are listed as undrawn until their design round.
* Gates: plan_sync selftest and check, contrast_check selftest and check.

**Depends on.** MA-186

issues.title: The Budget forecast shows each year's income, spend by category, EMIs, plans and surplus to the horizon, every figure traced to its flows, at every door
issues.description_html:
As the owner I want to see, year by year to the horizon, what comes in and what goes out, so that I can see how the plans change each year's budget, not only the net worth.

**Where.** `wealth/projection.py`'s budget forecast ledger; the Projection's Budget forecast tab at both doors (a route in `web/`, a SwiftUI piece in `ios/`); ARCHITECTURE.md 6.6, 9.3, 12.

**Acceptance.**

* Each year to the horizon (20 years by default; 5, 10, 20 or 30), expandable to its months: income by member, spend by category inflating by country and category, EMIs, each plan item, the surplus, the savings rate and closing cash, in GBP or INR, in today's money or not.
* Tapping any figure shows the flows that make it, from the engine's trace; the model never produces a number.
* The first month cash would go negative, a plan's funding running short, and the months below the admin's floor (a monthly surplus kept among the Projection's assumptions, GBP 500 to start, the admin's alone, holding while anyone in the household earns a salary; in retirement only cash running out is flagged) are flagged by code.
* Members see it; it moves on `records.changed` after every recalculation.
* Gates: pytest on the ledger (opening cash plus flows equals closing cash, every month), Playwright at 390 and 1440 in both themes, the iOS snapshot and accessibility checks; verified on dev.

**Design.** Picked on MA-264 (Arun, 28 Oct 2026): 1a, the surplus first. The tab opens on each year's leanest month against the floor, then the selected year's lines and its months, each figure opening its trace. Boards: Browser · Budget forecast 1a, the surplus first and iPhone · Budget forecast 1a, the surplus first, with their states on the 1a states boards (`docs/design/reviews/MA-264/decision.md`).

**Depends on.** MA-219, MA-222, MA-224

Filed on MA-261 (28 Oct 2026): future plans by talking. Designed on MA-264 (28 Oct 2026); Arun's floor and its rule in retirement settled there.

issues.title: When a plan leaves the household short, the agent proposes ways to rearrange the budget, and the admin's Confirm applies one, today's budget included
issues.description_html:
As the owner I want the agent to propose ways to cover a shortfall a plan causes, and apply the one I pick when I Confirm, so that the budget is rearranged the way Claude proposes a change and I accept it.

**Where.** The `rearrange_budget` tool and the goal-seek in `wealth/projection.py`; the scenario cards in the admin's chat at both doors; ARCHITECTURE.md 4.5, 4.10, 6.6, 8, 12.

**Acceptance.**

* When a plan leaves cash below zero or the surplus below the admin's floor (a monthly surplus kept among the Projection's assumptions, GBP 500 to start, the admin's alone, holding while anyone in the household earns a salary; in retirement only cash running out is flagged), code works out the options: trim a category from a date, pause or reduce a SIP, move a plan's start, draw from a named pool, change the surplus rule; each with its effect on every year, from the engine.
* The agent ranks and explains them; each opens as an unsaved scenario card.
* The admin's Confirm applies the chosen option: `change_flow` plan items from their dates and, where the option touches this month, the current month's budget plan; one audit row each, with Undo.
* Only the admin may apply one; a member asking sees the options and saves nothing.
* Gates: pytest on the goal-seek on hand-computed cases and on the admin-only refusals; an eval case per kind of option; verified on dev.

**Design.** Picked on MA-264 (Arun, 28 Oct 2026): 2a, a card per step. The plan is saved first with its own Confirm, then a Cover the gap card lists the ways, best fit first, each with its changes, its effect and its own Confirm, and two more folded. Boards: Browser · Plans in the chat 2a, a card per step and iPhone · Plans in the chat 2a, a card per step, with their states on the 2a states boards (`docs/design/reviews/MA-264/decision.md`).

**Depends on.** MA-96, MA-219, MA-222, MA-223

Filed on MA-261 (28 Oct 2026): future plans by talking. Arun: rearranging works "just like claude does", proposed then applied on Confirm. Designed on MA-264 (28 Oct 2026); Arun's floor and its rule in retirement settled there.

issues.title: Design the future-plans screens at every door: the Budget forecast, a plan made by talking, the budget rearranged on Confirm and the Plans tab, before anything is built

issues.title: The implementation stack, FastAPI, DynamoDB vs DocumentDB, the agent framework options, and end-to-end FastAPI and LLM observability with costing are researched and recorded in Confluence with block diagrams
issues.description_html:
As the owner and developer I want end-to-end AWS and LLM observability (including the FastAPI REST APIs and request IDs) researched with a costing analysis, and the detailed implementation stack across the web front end, the iOS app, the Python FastAPI and DynamoDB backend (including why not DocumentDB and which DynamoDB libraries to use), and the agent framework options compared and recommended, all recorded in the repo and in Confluence with block diagrams.

**Where.** `docs/RESEARCH.md` (§6), `TECH_STACK.md` (§1, §2, §3, §5), `ARCHITECTURE.md` (§3, §4.1, §4.8, §8, §10, §13, §16, §21.5), `PLAN.md`, `README.md`, `docs/design/README.md`, `docs/design/tech-stack-observability.html`, `docs/design/tech-stack-observability/*.gif`, `scripts/confluence_docs.py`, `scripts/confluence_record.py`, `docs/trace.json`, `docs/roadmap.json`, and Confluence (`stack` page and updated architecture record and phase pages).

* **Four-layer implementation stack:**
