    2. **iOS app:** React Native 0.88 bare (New Architecture, Fabric, TurboModules, Hermes, JSI, Swift Package Manager via `react-native spm`), TanStack Query 5.105 sharing `web/src/lib/` via Metro `#lib`, MMKV 4.3 on Nitro Modules, Reanimated 4.7, Gesture Handler 3.4, and a native Swift 6 SwiftUI core (`UIHostingController` inside Fabric view components, Swift Charts at 120 Hz ProMotion, Liquid Glass on controls only).

LangGraph, 5. Claude Agent SDK, 6. CrewAI / AutoGen) against ten MyPaisa requirements and recommends Option 1 (with PydanticAI / Strands patterns noted as alternatives).
    
* **Block diagrams and Confluence:** An interactive Warm ledger explainer page (`docs/design/tech-stack-observability.html`) with six animated block diagrams captured as GIFs and published to a dedicated Confluence page (`Tech stack, FastAPI, DynamoDB, agents and end-to-end observability`) alongside the updated Architecture Record pages.

issues.title: The api and stream Lambdas run FastAPI with Pydantic v2, request-id and trace correlation middleware, OpenTelemetry route spans, and generated OpenAPI TypeScript types shared by both doors
issues.description_html:
As the developer I want `handlers/api` and `handlers/stream` built as FastAPI applications with Pydantic v2 request and response contracts, request-id and W3C trace correlation middleware, OpenTelemetry route spans, and generated OpenAPI TypeScript types in `web/src/lib/`, so that every REST endpoint and the SSE stream share one typed contract with both doors and emit per-route telemetry from day one.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/api/app.py`, `src/mypaisa_agent/api/middleware.py`, `src/mypaisa_agent/handlers/api.py` (Mangum adapter), `src/mypaisa_agent/handlers/stream.py` (FastAPI on Uvicorn behind AWS Lambda Web Adapter 1.1 with `AWS_LWA_INVOKE_MODE=response_stream`), `scripts/openapi_export.py`, `web/src/lib/api-types.d.ts`, `tests/test_api_foundation.py`. ARCHITECTURE.md §8, §9.4, §9.5, §10.2, §10.3, §13, §16, §18.4, §21.5.

**Acceptance.**

* `handlers/api` runs a FastAPI application wrapped in `Mangum(app, lifespan="off")` for buffered REST endpoints (`GET /v1/app/minimum-version` with latest TestFlight build metadata for MA-167's minimum-version update prompt, `POST /v1/chat/messages`, `GET /v1/chat/turns`, `GET /v1/records`, `PATCH /v1/records/{id}`, `POST /v1/uploads`, `POST /v1/telemetry`, `/v1/admin/*`, `/v1/auth/*`), keeping cold start under 300 ms.
* `handlers/stream` runs a FastAPI application on Uvicorn behind AWS Lambda Web Adapter 1.1 (`AWS_LWA_INVOKE_MODE=response_stream`) for `GET /v1/stream` (`StreamingResponse` with `text/event-stream`). In `scripts/local/` (MA-198), both mount into one local Uvicorn ASGI process.
* `CorrelationMiddleware` extracts W3C `traceparent`, API Gateway's `request_id` (`aws_request_id` from the Lambda context or `x-amzn-requestid`), and `x-client-message-id`, binds `request_id`, `trace_id`, `span_id`, `run_id`, and the member's hash into `aws-lambda-powertools` Logger and the active OpenTelemetry span, and sets `x-mypaisa-trace-id` and `x-request-id` on every HTTP response (`2xx`, `4xx`, `5xx`), including FastAPI `RequestValidationError` (`422`) and unhandled exception handlers (`500`).
* `opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi` records a span per route using the route template (`http.route`, e.g. `POST /v1/chat/messages`, `PATCH /v1/records/{id}`, `GET /v1/stream`), feeding CloudWatch Application Signals per-operation latency and fault SLOs (`ARCHITECTURE.md` §10.2, §10.3).
* `scripts/openapi_export.py` exports FastAPI's OpenAPI 3.1 spec (`openapi.json`) without starting a server, and `openapi-typescript` generates `web/src/lib/api-types.d.ts`, imported by both the SvelteKit 3 web app and the React Native 0.88 iOS shell (`#lib`). A CI check fails if `api-types.d.ts` drifts from the FastAPI routes.
* Tests: middleware header propagation (`traceparent`, `x-mypaisa-trace-id`, `x-request-id`) on `200`, `202`, `422` and `500`; `GET /v1/app/minimum-version` schema and response; route template span attributes in the in-memory OTel exporter; OpenAPI schema export and TypeScript drift check.
* Gates: ruff, pyright, pytest; `pnpm check` in `web/`.

**Depends on.** MA-24, MA-29, MA-194, MA-265.

Updated 29 Oct 2026 (MA-274): adds `GET /v1/app/minimum-version` from Phase 1 for `MA-167`.

issues.title: Every pull request, container build and weekly schedule runs the seven-layer vulnerability gate across secrets, SAST, dependencies, Terraform and arm64 ECR images
issues.description_html:
## What and why

Before any application code or container image is promoted to `dev` or `prod`, every layer of the stack - secrets, static source (Python, TypeScript/SvelteKit, React Native, Swift), third-party dependencies, Terraform infrastructure-as-code, and the arm64 Lambda container images (`lambda` and `stream` targets) - must pass an automated vulnerability gate. Dependencies also gain newly disclosed CVEs when no commits happen, so a scheduled weekly scan and grouped Dependabot updates keep the repo clean between releases.

## Where in the repo

* `.github/workflows/pr-gates.yml` (security job)
* `.github/workflows/nightly-ops.yml` (weekly Monday 04:00 UTC full CVE sweep)
* `.github/dependabot.yml`
* `infra/bootstrap/codebuild.tf` (`trivy image` step in AWS CodeBuild arm64 buildspec + ECR Basic Scan on push)
* `scripts/security_scan.py` (local and CI unified runner)

## Acceptance criteria

* \[ \] **Gate 1 - Secrets (**`gitleaks`): Runs in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and on every PR over the commit range; fails on any AWS key, Anthropic key, JWT, APNs `.p8`, or high-entropy secret.
* \[ \] **Gate 2 - SAST (**`ruff` Bandit `S` + `semgrep` + `eslint-plugin-security`): Runs on every PR across Python (`src/`), TypeScript (`web/`, `ios/`), and Swift (`ios/MyPaisa/`); fails on injection patterns, unsafe deserialization, missing `Depends(require_member)` on protected FastAPI routes, or insecure Keychain/WebView flags.
* \[ \] **Gate 3 - SCA / Dependency Audit:** Runs `uv lock --check` and `pip-audit --strict` for Python, `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` for web/RN, and `trivy fs --scanners vuln --severity HIGH,CRITICAL ios/` for Swift `Package.resolved` and CocoaPods lockfiles.
* \[ \] **Gate 4 - IaC Security (**`tflint` + `trivy config`): Scans `infra/` for unencrypted resources, missing S3 `PublicAccessBlock`, wildcard IAM policies, and verifies that every `aws_ssm_parameter` of type `SecureString` uses `value_wo` and `value_wo_version` (`MA-159`).
* \[ \] **Gate 5 - Container Image CVE Gate (**`trivy image` + ECR Scan on Push): Runs inside AWS CodeBuild `arm1.small` immediately after building `mypaisa:lambda-<sha>` and `mypaisa:stream-<sha>` (`MA-237`); fails the build before deployment if any Critical or High CVE with an available fix (`--ignore-unfixed`) is present in either image.
* \[ \] **Gate 6 - Weekly Scheduled CVE Sweep & Dependabot:** `.github/workflows/nightly-ops.yml` runs the full SCA and ECR image scan every Monday at 04:00 UTC and alerts via GitHub Issues / SNS if a newly published High/Critical CVE affects `main`.

## Gates

* `python3 scripts/plan_sync.py selftest && python3 scripts/plan_sync.py check`
* `python3 scripts/security_scan.py --all`

issues.title: A phase-progressive smoke runner checks every deployment in dev and prod, protects prod from synthetic writes, verifies the X-Ray trace in dev, and rolls back prod on failure
issues.description_html:
## What and why

`MA-107` and `MA-232` require smoke tests after `dev` and `prod` deployments, with automatic rollback if `prod` fails, while `.claude/rules/aws-changes.md` forbids any script from writing synthetic records into `prod` DynamoDB tables. We need a single phase-progressive smoke test runner (`scripts/smoke.py`) that runs full synthetic round-trip and X-Ray trace assertions in `dev` and strictly read-only, non-mutating health, auth-perimeter, and CloudWatch alarm checks in `prod`, triggering instant Lambda `:live` alias and CloudFront rollback on failure.

## Where in the repo

* `scripts/smoke.py`
* `.github/workflows/release.yml`
* `tests/test_smoke_runner.py`

## Acceptance criteria

* \[ \] **Phase-progressive CLI (**`scripts/smoke.py --env dev|prod --up-to-phase <N>`): Runs in under 45 seconds and activates the checks for every completed phase up to `N`.
* \[ \] **Health & Deep Infrastructure Probe (Both** `dev` and `prod`): Asserts `GET /v1/health` returns `200` with `git_sha == $GITHUB_SHA`, and `GET /v1/health?deep=1` verifies read-only DynamoDB (`DescribeTable`), S3 (`HeadBucket`), SQS (`GetQueueAttributes`), and SSM/KMS connectivity without mutating state.
* \[ \] **Web Door & Universal Links (Both** `dev` and `prod`): Verifies `dashboard(-dev).mypaisapp.com` returns `200`, HSTS/CSP headers, and valid `.well-known/apple-app-site-association` JSON.
* \[ \] **OpenAPI Auth Perimeter (Both** `dev` and `prod`): Calls every protected route in `/openapi.json` without credentials and asserts `401 Unauthorized`.
* \[ \] **Full Synthetic Round-Trip & X-Ray Trace Assertion (**`dev` only): Signs in as the synthetic `dev` smoke member, opens `GET /v1/stream` SSE, posts a deterministic zero-cost `smoke-ping` turn to `POST /v1/chat/messages`, verifies the `RunRecord`, and polls `aws xray batch-get-traces` to assert one unbroken trace across `api` -> SQS -> `agent` -> `sender` (`MA-232`).
* \[ \] **Prod Read-Only Safety & Instant Auto-Rollback:** Never writes a record, message, or `RunRecord` in `prod`; if any `prod` check fails or `mypaisa-prod-lambda-errors` enters `ALARM`, `.github/workflows/release.yml` shifts all `mypaisa-prod-*` `:live` aliases back to their previous versions in under 5 seconds, restores the S3 web manifest, and alerts via SNS.

## Gates

* `python3 scripts/plan_sync.py selftest && python3 scripts/plan_sync.py check`
* `pytest tests/test_smoke_runner.py`

issues.title: A five-layer regression pyramid and path-filtered CI runner test units, OpenAPI contracts, moto integration, golden maths, web and iOS UI, and T0 agent replays inside the free minute tiers
issues.description_html:
## What and why

As phases 0 through 20 land across Python, FastAPI, SvelteKit 3, React Native, SwiftUI, and the Claude agent harness, we need a unified five-layer regression pyramid (`scripts/regression.py`) and path-filtered GitHub Actions matrix (`Option D`) that catches regressions at every layer - unit/property tests, OpenAPI contract drift, Maestro YAML syntax and selector parity, local `moto` ASGI integration, golden financial maths, web/iOS visual & accessibility checks, and `T0` deterministic agent replays - while keeping monthly GitHub Actions, AWS CodeBuild, and Argos CI usage inside the £0 free tiers.

## Where in the repo

* `scripts/regression.py`
* `.github/workflows/pr-gates.yml` and `.github/workflows/web-visual-a11y.yml`
* `web/tests/helpers/audit-and-capture.ts`
* `tests/golden/` (wealth-tracker and trading-desk golden maths fixtures)

## Acceptance criteria

* \[ \] **Layer 1 - Unit, Property-Based (**`hypothesis`), Maestro Syntax & OpenAPI Contract Gate: Runs `ruff`, `pyright`, `pytest` (unit + Hypothesis), `svelte-check`, `vitest`, iOS `Jest`, `python3 scripts/maestro_local.py check-syntax` (looping one file per invocation across `.maestro/subflows/*.yaml` and `.maestro/flows/*.yaml` plus `TestIDs.swift` <-> `web/src/lib/test-ids.ts` selector parity, `MA-273`), and exports FastAPI's `/openapi.json` to assert zero diff against generated TypeScript client types (`openapi-typescript`, `MA-266`) on every PR (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`, 1x).
* \[ \] **Layer 2 - Full-Stack Local Integration (**`moto` + FastAPI ASGI): Tests multi-Lambda workflows (`api` -> SQS -> `agent` -> `DynamoDB TransactWriteItems` -> `sender` -> `stream` SSE) in-memory against the seeded household (`MA-110`, `MA-198`).
* \[ \] **Layer 3 - Deterministic Agent Replay (**`T0`) & Golden Maths Fixtures: Runs Inspect AI `T0` recorded cassettes (`MA-246` to `MA-249`), the PII-leak span/log check (`MA-232`), and the golden financial calculation fixtures (646 wealth-tracker cases + 11 trading-desk indicator series) on every PR.
* \[ \] **Layer 4 - Path-Filtered Web & iOS Visual and Accessibility Suite:** Runs `board_fit.js` and `contrast_check.py` as repo-local, zero-quota board gates when `docs/design/**` changes; on the built SvelteKit 3 (`web/`) code when `web/**` or `cards/**` change (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`, 1x, `concurrency: cancel-in-progress`), runs Playwright 1.64 at `390x844` and `1440x900` in `.t-light` and `.t-dark` (plus privacy mode `£••••` on wealth/home screens) through one shared `auditAndCapture()` fixture executing deterministic stabilization, fail-closed `@axe-core/playwright` 4.14 WCAG 2.2 Level A & AA before capture, keyboard focus/landmark checks (`MA-181`), and **Argos CI** (`@argos-ci/playwright`, Tokenless GitHub App OIDC, `uploadToArgos: !!process.env.CI`) capturing cloud visual PNG diffs in both themes (`threshold: 0.2`) and a light-theme-deduplicated YAML `ariaSnapshot` accessibility tree (\~3,600 snapshots/month inside the 5,000/month £0 Free Hobby tier, `docs/RESEARCH.md` §10, `docs/design/argos-visual-a11y.html`); runs iOS `Jest` on Linux (1x) and gates native SwiftUI `XCTest`/`XCUITest`/Snapshot/AX5 (`macos-15` or self-hosted Mac runner) to `ios/**` and `cards/**` changes plus `main` releases, paired locally on Apple Silicon with `python3 scripts/maestro_local.py --up-to-phase <N>` across the 5-simulator pool (`MA-273`, £0/month).
* \[ \] **Layer 5 - Change-Gated Live Evals (**`T1` / `T2`): Triggers `T1` (`MA-250`) only when prompts, tools, guards, kind templates, or model routing change, and `T2` (`MA-251`) on model version upgrades.

## Gates

* `python3 scripts/plan_sync.py selftest && python3 scripts/plan_sync.py check`
* `python3 scripts/regression.py --layer 1,2,3`

Updated 29 Oct 2026 (MA-274): adds L1 `maestro_local.py check-syntax` + `TestIDs` parity and L4 local Apple Silicon `maestro_local.py` (`MA-273`). Updated 30 Oct 2026: folds in the Argos CI + Playwright 1.64 + `@axe-core/playwright` WCAG 2.2 AA + light-deduplicated YAML `ariaSnapshot` pipeline (`docs/RESEARCH.md` §10, `docs/design/argos-visual-a11y.html`) inside the £0/month Free Hobby tier.

issues.title: A typed DynamoDB single-table repository wraps boto3 TypeSerializer, mypy-boto3-dynamodb and TransactWriteUnit with Pydantic v2 marshaling, scan guard and signed cursor pagination
issues.description_html:
## What and why

`MA-265` (`docs/RESEARCH.md` §6.2) evaluated DynamoDB vs DocumentDB and selected Amazon DynamoDB (On-Demand) with a thin, strictly typed Python single-table repository built on `Pydantic v2`, `boto3` (`TypeSerializer`/`TypeDeserializer`), `mypy-boto3-dynamodb` (`boto3-stubs[dynamodb]`), and a `TransactWriteUnit` transaction builder across `mypaisa-<env>` (`Record`, `Event`, `View`, `AuditEvent`). This setup story builds that repository foundation before `MA-27` and `MA-28` implement the household's domain records and hash-chained audit log.

## Where in the repo

* `src/mypaisa_agent/registry/keys.py`
* `src/mypaisa_agent/registry/serde.py`
* `src/mypaisa_agent/registry/client.py`
* `src/mypaisa_agent/registry/uow.py`
* `tests/test_dynamodb_repository.py`

## Acceptance criteria

* \[ \] **Typed Key Builders & Wire Serializer (**`keys.py`, `serde.py`): Converts Pydantic v2 domain models cleanly to and from DynamoDB `AttributeValue` maps via `TypeSerializer`/`TypeDeserializer`, preserving `Decimal` minor-unit precision, rejecting raw IEEE `float` on money fields, and enforcing `mypy-boto3-dynamodb` strict typing.
* \[ \] **Scan Guard (**`client.py`): Wraps `DynamoDBClient` and raises `ForbiddenScanError` if `.scan()` or `.scan_paginator()` is ever called (`MA-27`).
* \[ \] **Atomic Unit of Work (**`TransactWriteUnit` in `uow.py`): Executes atomic writes of `Record` + `Event` + `View` + hash-chained `AuditEvent` (`prev_hash` -> `row_hash`) + `IdempotencyKey` in one `transact_write_items` call, translating `TransactionCanceledException` `CancellationReasons` into typed domain errors (`OptimisticLockError`, `DuplicateIdempotencyKeyError`, `AuditChainMismatchError`).
* \[ \] **Optimistic Concurrency & Signed Cursor Pagination:** Enforces `version` increments on every mutable item and encodes/decodes DynamoDB `LastEvaluatedKey` into URL-safe, HMAC-signed opaque cursor tokens for FastAPI pagination.
* \[ \] **OpenTelemetry DynamoDB Spans:** Records table name, operation, item count, and `ReturnConsumedCapacity='TOTAL'` read/write capacity units on the active OTel span without logging attribute values or financial amounts.

## Gates

* `python3 scripts/plan_sync.py selftest && python3 scripts/plan_sync.py check`
* `pytest tests/test_dynamodb_repository.py`

issues.title: A typed AnthropicAgentRunner loop manages prompt caching for every agent (three explicit breakpoints and automatic caching for the tail), the Pydantic v2 tool registry, policy and figure hooks, and gen_ai OpenTelemetry spans
issues.description_html:
## What and why

`MA-265` evaluated six agent frameworks and selected a thin, custom-typed `AnthropicAgentRunner` (\~250 lines of Python over `anthropic.AsyncAnthropic` + Pydantic v2) for the interactive `agent` Lambda. That keeps first-class control over:

* prompt caching for every agent (`cache_control={"type": "ephemeral"}`, ARCHITECTURE 24.1);
* PDF document blocks and citations;
* the in-loop policy gate (`MA-247`) and the post-loop figure validator (`MA-248`);
* `gen_ai.*` OpenTelemetry spans (`MA-233`).

This story builds that core runner and `@tool` schema registry. Every later agent is built on it, so caching and memory come from here (ARCHITECTURE 24, MA-285).

## Where in the repo

* `src/mypaisa/agent/runner.py`
* `src/mypaisa/agent/tools.py`
* `src/mypaisa/agent/cache.py`
* `tests/test_agent_runner.py`

## Acceptance criteria

* \[ \] **Typed** `@tool` **Registry & Pydantic v2 Schema Export.** Declares every tool with `@tool(agents=[...], scope="read"|"propose"|"write", allowed_when_tainted=bool)` and generates strict JSON Schemas matching the manifest checked by `MA-246`.
* \[ \] **Prompt Cache Assembler, for every agent** (ARCHITECTURE 24.1, updated 29 Oct 2026 by MA-285).

    * Builds every request in one frozen order: tools sorted by name and serialised deterministically, then the system prompt with the kind templates, then the messages.
    * Places at most three explicit `cache_control={"type": "ephemeral"}` breakpoints: (1) the tools and system prompt together, (2) the household structure snapshot, (3) the conversation notes.
    * Leaves the fourth slot to the request's top-level automatic caching for the conversation's tail; four explicit breakpoints plus automatic caching would be a 400.
    * Takes each agent's cache lifetime from its manifest (the chat's fixed part 1h, its tail 5m).
    * Keeps the warm-turn cache hit ratio above 75%. MA-286 adds the byte test, T1's read check and the panel's alarm.
    
* \[ \] **Async Tool-Use Loop with Policy & Figure Hooks.** Runs the `messages.stream` / `messages.create` loop up to the per-run step cap. Passes every `tool_use` block through the policy gate (`MA-247`) before execution, runs the figure validator (`MA-248`) on the final reply before emitting to `mypaisa-<env>-out.fifo`, and enforces the monthly budget ceiling (`MA-113`).
* \[ \] **Automatic** `gen_ai.*` **&** `mypaisa.*` **Span Emission.** Wraps every model turn and tool call in OpenTelemetry spans. Each records the model ID, input and output tokens, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `ttft_ms`, `cost_usd` and `stop_reason`, with zero message content (`MA-233`).

## Gates

* `python3 scripts/plan_sync.py selftest && python3 scripts/plan_sync.py check`
* `pytest tests/test_agent_runner.py`

issues.title: E9: the Budget forecast and the Projection are graded against every closed month, and their assumptions learn from the household's own history on the admin's Confirm
issues.description_html:
As the owner I want each month's Budget forecast and the Projection checked against what really happened, and their assumptions tuned from our own history, so that the plan gets closer to our real life every month without anything changing behind my back.

**Arun's words, 29 Oct 2026.** "I need the entire app to be self learning based on my needs, the data tracked in database and S3 storage for all processing to calibrate and tune the system."

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/wealth/` (the grader and the tuner beside `projection.py`), the month close (MA-220), the settings service (MA-129), the admin's chat and the Projection's assumptions panel at both doors; `ARCHITECTURE.md` 20.9 and 6.6.

**Acceptance.**

* At each month close, code grades that month's line of the Budget forecast run that was current on its 1st: income by member, spend by category, EMIs, each plan item, the surplus and closing cash. Each gap is a `MonthGrade` row, in money and as a percentage, traced to the input it comes from. Once a year it also grades the Projection's net worth from a year earlier. A late statement regrades its month with a new row; none is overwritten.
* The tuner refits only inputs that are estimates (a category's run rate against its plan, a category's own inflation blended with its country's prior by years of history, a member's salary growth), never the household's facts. It proposes a new value only with at least 6 closed months behind it, only when that value would have forecast the months in its window (the last 12, or as many as have closed) better than the current one by more than its margin, and moves it at most one step. The window, the minimum, the margin and the step are settings.
* A proposal is a card in the admin's chat and on the Projection's assumptions panel: the assumption from and to, the months that show it, what it does to the surplus and to net worth at 20 years, and Undo. It is applied only on the admin's Confirm, as a new version of the assumptions with its audit row; like a plan item it changes a plan, not the records, so it needs no second check. Members see it and cannot apply it. A rejected proposal is not offered again for its setting's period; an applied one whose next three months grade worse is offered back.
* The records, the budget plan and the engine's arithmetic never change: the same inputs give the same Budget forecast to the penny, and every learned value is a versioned assumption.
* The Budget forecast tab shows each closed month's forecast beside its actual, at every door. Designed first with /design-first before the story starts.
* Gates: unit and property tests (a regrade gives the same grade; no proposal before 6 closed months; a proposal never writes a record or the plan), the plan-sync gate, `board_fit.js` for its boards.

**Depends on.** MA-219, MA-220, MA-262, MA-129.

**Where.** The agent and its run records (`ARCHITECTURE.md` 10.1), the statement reader's merchant memory (MA-218), the extractor's cases (`ARCHITECTURE.md` 23.5), preferences (MA-69), You and the Admin center at both doors; `ARCHITECTURE.md` 20.9.

**Acceptance.**

* Learned for each member from that member's own taps, answers, corrections and mutes only, never from text a file, a page, a search or the news brought in.
* On its own, inside its band: the order of the composer's chips and of each screen's Ask, and the order of the brief's sections.
* At the member's Confirm: a merchant's category, from a correction on a statement's review card; an alert threshold, a quiet hour or a check-in's usual answer, proposed as a preference card when the pattern holds (an alert muted five times, the same answer three months running).
* A field a member corrects on a Confirm card after a file becomes a case on the synthetic household, and a regression case on the admin's Confirm behind the second check (`ARCHITECTURE.md` 23.5).
* Never a record, a figure, a stance, a forecast or a setting outside its band. Each member's learning is their own; You lists what was learned, with a reset; the admin sees the household's in the Admin center.
* Counts only, never message text, kept in DynamoDB and under the household's prefix in the lake.
* Designed first with /design-first before the story starts.
* Gates: tests that untrusted text teaches nothing, that one member's learning never reaches another, and that nothing outside the band changes without a Confirm; the plan-sync gate; `board_fit.js` for its boards.

**Depends on.** MA-129, MA-218, MA-69, MA-246.

issues.title: Optional AWS VPC enterprise lockdown and seven-layer data perimeter across dev and prod, decided last
issues.description_html:
As the operator I want an optional seven-layer AWS VPC enterprise lockdown and Data Perimeter across dev and prod in us-east-1 (with Option 3B Lean Zero-Trust VPC preferred at +£24.86/month inside the £50/month AWS cap, and Options 1, 2A, 2B and 3A documented for comparison) so that I can decide last, after Phase 20, whether to switch MyPaisa from serverless IAM/tag isolation to full private-network and aws:SourceVpce Data Perimeter isolation without redesigning the application.

**Where.** `infra/modules/mypaisa/vpc.tf`, `infra/modules/mypaisa/data_perimeter.tf`, `infra/modules/mypaisa/dns_firewall.tf`, `infra/modules/mypaisa/egress_nat.tf`, `infra/dev/`, `infra/prod/`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, `scripts/smoke.py`, `docs/RESEARCH.md`
**Acceptance.**

* Controlled by an explicit Terraform toggle (`enable_vpc_lockdown = false` by default until Arun decides after Phase 20); while off, `dev` and `prod` keep the £3.50/month serverless-native IAM/tag isolation of `ARCHITECTURE.md` §14 and §18.1.
* Layer 1 (Topology and blast-radius blocks): non-overlapping dual-stack VPCs for `mypaisa-dev-vpc` (`10.10.0.0/16`) and `mypaisa-prod-vpc` (`10.20.0.0/16`) in `us-east-1` with zero VPC peering, three subnet tiers per AZ (Isolated zero-egress, Private egress, Perimeter), default VPCs absent, IAM region lock to `us-east-1`, AWS VPC Block Public Access (`Ingress-only` on egress VPCs, `Bidirectional` on isolated VPCs), S3 and EBS Snapshot Block Public Access, and IMDSv2 enforced (`HttpTokens = required`, hop limit `1`).
* Layer 2 (Front-door ingress lockdown): `dashboard` S3 locked to CloudFront Origin Access Control (`SigV4` + `aws:SourceArn`) with `SecurityHeadersPolicy`; `api` and `/v1/stream` SSE locked behind CloudFront (Option 3B preferred: CloudFront Pro flat-rate plan bundling AWS WAF and DDoS on `prod`, Free plan on `dev`, Regional API Gateway with `disable_execute_api_endpoint = true` and mTLS/origin-secret verification; Option 1 alternative documented: CloudFront VPC Origins to Internal ALB).
* Layer 3 (Private AWS backbone and three-way Data Perimeter): free S3 and DynamoDB Gateway VPC Endpoints plus optional PrivateLink Interface Endpoints; S3, DynamoDB, KMS and SQS resource policies enforce Network Perimeter (`aws:SourceVpce` `Deny` with surgical `aws:ViaAWSService` and CI role carve-outs), Resource Perimeter (`aws:ResourceAccount = 545595341442` on endpoint policies against data exfiltration) and Identity Perimeter (`aws:PrincipalAccount`).
* Layer 4 (Outbound filtering and micro-segmentation): deterministic engine and quarantined file-extractor Lambdas run in Isolated zero-egress subnets (`sg-lambda-isolated`, zero `0.0.0.0/0` route); external-calling Lambdas (`api`, `agent`, `auth`, `ingester`, `notifier`) run in Private Egress subnets (`sg-lambda-egress` allowing outbound TCP `443` only, blocking raw DNS `53`/`853`, SSH `22` and SMTP `25`) behind Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall in default-deny (`*` -> `NXDOMAIN`) mode allowlisting only required FQDNs, paired in preferred Option 3B with IPv6 EIGW (£0) and auto-healing Graviton `t4g.nano` `fck-nat` / Envoy TLS-SNI egress proxies (+£11.32/month across `dev` and `prod`).
* Layer 5 (Private CI/CD and zero-bastion access): `arm64` AWS CodeBuild runners attach to private egress subnets to build images, push to ECR, apply Terraform and run private smoke checks inside the perimeter via GitHub Actions OIDC; zero SSH port `22` or public bastions (break-glass via SSM Session Manager over PrivateLink, IAM + MFA + S3 session audit).
* Layer 6 and 7 (Telemetry, verification and safe rollout): enriched v5 VPC Flow Logs, Route 53 Resolver Query/Block Logs and WAF/CloudFront logs delivered to KMS-encrypted S3 with `aws:SourceArn`/`aws:SourceAccount` confused-deputy guards, GuardDuty, IAM External Access Analyzer (£0), VPC Reachability Analyzer CI check, and a five-step zero-lockout rollout order (Alert-only -> Enforce) keeping total AWS spend at \~£28.36/month under the £50/month cap in Option 3B.
* Gates: `terraform validate`, `tflint`, `trivy config`, `plan-sync`, `smoke` (`dev` full + X-Ray, `prod` strictly read-only), and VPC Reachability Analyzer verification.

issues.title: Every agent's model calls are cached automatically: a frozen prefix, a lifetime per route, automatic caching for the tail, and an alarm when reads fall
issues.description_html:
As the admin I want every agent MyPaisa builds to cache its prompt without anyone remembering to, so that each call pays for its fixed part once and the Claude budget lasts.

**What.** The runner (`AnthropicAgentRunner`, MA-271) makes the request for every agent, so caching lives there once (ARCHITECTURE 24.1):

* **One order, frozen.** Tools sorted by name and serialised deterministically, then the system prompt, then the messages. Nothing that changes per member, per day or per request sits before the first breakpoint: no date, no member name, no id, no figure, no unsorted JSON.
* **Dynamic context goes after the cache.** Today's date, the member's name and mode, privacy mode and the ladder's step arrive as a mid-conversation system message, after the cached prefix. Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 support this with no beta.
* **Breakpoints.** At most three explicit breakpoints at the stable layers: tools and system together, then the household's layer, then the notes. Top-level automatic caching (`cache_control` on the request) takes the conversation's tail, the fourth slot.
* **A lifetime per route.** Each agent's manifest (MA-246) names its time to live from how far apart its calls start. Under 5 minutes takes 5m; 5 to 60 minutes takes 1h, longer first. The chat's fixed part is 1h, as ARCHITECTURE 8 says, and its tail 5m. A daily or weekly run takes 5m within the run. Batches mark their shared prefix too.
* **One model per loop.** Caches belong to a model, so a loop never switches models mid-run. A cheaper sub-task is its own call.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/agent/cache.py` and `runner.py`, each agent's manifest, the model panel and its alarms (MA-233), the T1 golden set (MA-250).

**Acceptance.**

* A unit test builds every agent's request twice (two members, two days, two runs) and asserts the bytes before the first breakpoint are identical. No date, id, name, figure or unsorted key leaks in.
* A manifest with no time to live, or more than three explicit breakpoints, fails the build.
* In T1 (evals workspace), the second identical request of each agent shows `cache_read_input_tokens` above zero.
* Every `RunRecord` holds the cache read and write tokens per call. The model panel shows the cache-read share per agent. An alarm fires once when an agent's share falls out of its band for a day.
* In dev, cache diagnostics (beta `cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07`, Claude API only) names where a broken prefix first differs.
* The Console's caching analytics for the dev and prod workspaces show reads once traffic runs. That is the second place to look, beside the panel.

**Depends on.** MA-271, MA-233, MA-246, MA-250.

**Gates.** `uv run ruff check . && uv run pyright && uv run pytest`; T1 on the change.

issues.title: Every agent keeps memory across runs through Claude's memory tool on MyPaisa's own store, scoped, guarded and audited, and long runs stay lean
issues.description_html:
As a member I want MyPaisa to remember what I told it last week, such as how I like answers and what I am planning, without my repeating it. As the admin I want that memory never to hold a figure, a secret or someone else's detail, and never to push the Claude bill past its ceiling.

**What** (ARCHITECTURE 24.2 to 24.6).

* **The tool.** The runner gives every agent Claude's memory tool (`memory_20250818`). Its six commands (view, create, str_replace, insert, delete, rename) run against MyPaisa's own store, `MemoryNote` rows in the one DynamoDB table, never a local disk.
* **Scopes.** Each agent has three:

    * `/memories/<agent>/members/<member_id>/`: one member's notes, read only in that member's own runs, the owner's included;
    * `/memories/<agent>/household/`: shared notes, read by every member's runs, so they hold nothing private;
    * `/memories/<agent>/self/`: the agent's own working notes.  
      An agent's manifest (MA-246) grants which scopes it may read and write. The policy gate (MA-247) checks each command like any tool call.
    
* **What a note may hold.** Plain words about the person and the work: how a member likes answers, what they are planning, what they asked MyPaisa to keep in mind.

    * Never a figure or a record. A note holds no amount, balance, rate, percentage, account or card number, id, token or secret. The write handler refuses each in code. Records live in the registry through Confirm; a note may name a record but never holds its values.
    * The figure check (MA-248) matches figures only against tool results and the member's own words, so a figure from a note cannot reach a reply.
    * Never a setting. Behaviour stays in the settings store (ARCHITECTURE 20.2) and the member's preferences.
    
* **Written by the agent, seen by the member.** The agent writes notes on its own as well as when a member says "remember". Every write is an audit row (`memory.write`, the path and the run) and one line in Activity, "MyPaisa noted: ...". The member reads, corrects and forgets their notes in You (MA-288).
* **Guarded.**

    * A run that has read untrusted text (ARCHITECTURE 23.2) cannot write memory: the gate refuses every writing command there, delete included.
    * Notes are read as data, never as an instruction.
    
* **Lifetime.** A note is kept until the member forgets it or leaves the household (MA-172 deletes their notes), with no expiry.
* **Within the budget** (ARCHITECTURE 24.6).

    * The runner loads a run's notes once, at its start, into the cached notes layer (the third breakpoint, MA-271, MA-286). Every later message reads them at a tenth of the input price, about half a penny to write per conversation and a twentieth of a penny a message after it on Sonnet 5.5. A note written mid-run applies from the next run, so the history stays append-only.
    * Caps: at most 2,000 tokens of a member's notes per agent, 1,000 for the household and 3,000 for an agent's own; at most two writes a run, counted in the run's eight-call guard. A write past a cap is refused with the reason.
    * Every memory read and write is costed under its own feature, `memory`, in the cycle's `SpendMonth`, and the model panel shows it.
    * The ladder (ARCHITECTURE 15.1): from 85% a note is written only when a member asks; from 95% notes are read and none written; at 100% Claude stops and notes wait unchanged.
    
* **Lean within a run.** A long tool run (the Saturday review, an ops repair) uses server-side context editing (`clear_tool_uses_20250919`, beta `context-management-2025-06-27`) to drop old tool results. A conversation past its limit starts afresh from a summary, as ARCHITECTURE 8 says. Neither edits the stored history.

**Where.** `src/mypaisa_agent/agent/memory.py`, `registry/` (`MemoryNote`), the policy gate, `audit.py`, the meter (`memory` feature), each agent's manifest, the golden set.

**Acceptance.**

* A note written in one conversation is used in the next one of the same member, and never in another member's, the owner's included.
* The write handler refuses an amount, a percentage, an account number, a token and a secret, each a test.
* A run that read a file or a fetched page writes no note, and the refusal is on its span.
* A household note shows in both members' runs.
* Each write is an audit row and an Activity line. Forgetting removes the note's text and keeps the audit row without it.
* Leaving the household deletes the member's notes.
* The second message of a conversation reads the notes layer from the cache (`cache_read_input_tokens` covers it). A note over its cap, and a third write in a run, are refused.
* The meter books memory under `memory`. At a mocked 85% a note is written only on "remember", and at 95% none is.
* T1 has memory cases: recall, the figure refusal, the tainted run, another member's scope.
* Context editing on a long recorded run keeps the request under its limit, and the history replays byte for byte.

**Settled** (Arun, 29 Oct 2026: "go for all recommended options, I need the app to grow and remember me. But it should not exceed costs"):

1. Who reads a member's notes: only that member's own runs.
2. How long a note is kept: until forgotten or the member leaves, with no expiry.
3. Whether the agent writes notes on its own: yes, each shown in Activity.

**Depends on.** MA-271, MA-286, MA-246, MA-247, MA-248, MA-113, MA-115, MA-172.

**Gates.** `uv run ruff check . && uv run pyright && uv run pytest`; T1 on the change; the safety suite.

issues.title: A member sees what MyPaisa remembers about them and corrects or forgets it, in You, at both doors
issues.description_html:
As a member I want to see everything MyPaisa has noted about me, and to correct a note or make it forget one, so that what it remembers stays mine.

**What** (ARCHITECTURE 24.3).

* **The page.** You gains What MyPaisa remembers, in the iOS app and in the web app. It shows the member's own notes from every agent, grouped by agent, each with when it was written and from which conversation. It also shows the household's shared notes, marked shared. Nobody else's notes appear, the owner's view included.
* **Correct in place.** Tap a note, change its words, and a before and after line appears with Save. Save writes through the memory store with an audit row (`via: inline_edit`), as ARCHITECTURE 1's rule 4 asks of any correction. Nothing is added here: a new note comes only from the chat, from the agent on its own or on "remember that ...".
* **Forget.** Forget one note, or all of a member's notes, with a Confirm. The text is removed for good, and the audit row stays without it. A note never expires on its own.
* **Shared notes.** The owner corrects or forgets the household's shared notes. A member can ask in the chat for one to change.
* **Activity.** Each "MyPaisa noted: ..." line, written as the agent notes something, opens its note.
* **Privacy mode** changes nothing here: a note holds no figure.

**Design.** No board yet. The page, a note's correction, forget one and forget all, an empty state and a long list are drawn with /design-first before the story starts. They are drawn at desktop, 390, iPhone and iPad, in light and dark, in the same round as MA-277's list in You of what was learned, so You has one place for both.

**Acceptance.**

* The page shows exactly the member's own notes and the household's, never another member's.
* A correction shows its before and after with Save, and writes one audit row.
* Forget all needs Confirm and leaves no text behind.
* Each Activity line opens its note.
* Built from the picked boards at both doors, in light and dark, legible at 25% brightness.

**Settled** (Arun, 29 Oct 2026: "go for all recommended options, I need the app to grow and remember me. But it should not exceed costs"):

1. A member's notes are read only in their own runs.
2. A note is kept until forgotten or the member leaves.
3. The agent writes notes on its own, each shown in Activity.

**Depends on.** MA-287, MA-277 (drawn together), MA-170 (You).

**Gates.** The iOS gates (MA-166), Playwright at 390 and 1440 in both themes, `contrast_check.py`.

issues.title: Each agent of the team keeps notes of what it tried, what worked and what the admin decided, read at the start of each run and never a second settings store
issues.description_html:
As the admin I want each agent of the team to remember its own past runs, so that it does not repeat a failed fix, re-propose what I rejected, or rediscover a source's quirk every night.

**What** (ARCHITECTURE 24.4).

* **Its own scope.** Each agent of ARCHITECTURE 20.1 gets the memory of the phase 1 story in its `self` scope:

    * the data steward: each source's quirks and outages;
    * the news scout: feeds that went bad;
    * the Forecaster: what its explanations got wrong;
    * the grader and tuner: why the admin approved or rejected each change request, so a rejected request is not proposed again within its setting's period;
    * the ops warden: each incident, what it tried and what fixed it;
    * the admin desk: how the admin likes requests batched.
    
* **Read first.** A run reads its notes with `view` at its start, after the cached prefix.
* **Never a setting.** A note can say what worked. Changing behaviour still goes through a setting inside its band or a change request the admin approves (ARCHITECTURE 20.2, 20.3).
* **Never a figure.** The same refusals as the phase 1 story apply.
* **Visible to the admin.** The Admin center lists each agent's notes, which the admin reads, corrects or clears, behind the second check, with an audit row.
* **Guarded** as in phase 1. An agent that read fetched or uploaded text in a run writes no note in it (ARCHITECTURE 23.2). Each agent's manifest (MA-256) names its scopes.

**Acceptance.**

* The ops warden, given a recorded incident it fixed before, tries the fix that worked first, and its notes say why.
* A change request the admin rejected is not proposed again within its period, and the note says so.
* A note never changes a setting: a test tries and is refused.
* The Admin center lists, corrects and clears notes behind the second check.

**Design.** The Admin center's notes list is drawn with /design-first in MA-279's consolidated Admin center before the story starts.

**Depends on.** The phase 1 memory story, MA-256, MA-129, MA-130.

**Gates.** `uv run ruff check . && uv run pyright && uv run pytest`; each agent's safety suite (MA-256).

issues.title: Prototype v5: one clickable walk-through of the whole journey, phases 0 to 20, at every door, with stubbed figures
issues.description_html:
As Arun I want one consolidated clickable prototype that runs the whole MyPaisa journey end to end, phases 0 to 20, at the web app on desktop and at 390, the iPhone app, and the iPad and foldable, all from stubbed figures, so that I can understand and check the whole product in one place before anything more is built.

Arun's ask, 29 Oct 2026: "build full end to end working prototype for web, mobile and ios with all mocked and stubbed data. It should cover all the scenarios across all phases from 0 to 20, including forecast, projection, stock shares predictions, users chatting and entering assets, holdings forecast, buy/sell/add signal, news and events sentiment analysis results ... Some of the designs were done 4 days back which had holdings, track record for the holdings. But after merging wealth and stuffs, it drifted." And: do not drift from (1) an intelligent self-learning recommendation system for stocks, shares, ETFs and funds, (2) built on rules and past data, with agents that come up with the engines.

Arun's choices, 29 Oct 2026: a clickable prototype in docs/design (a design record, not product code); every door (desktop web, phone web, iPhone, iPad and foldable); the screens that drifted or were never drawn are drawn straight into the prototype in the v4 design, following the picks already made (shell 1a, the dashboard 1a, the check-in card 1b, the Projection 1a, the Forecast tab 1a), each marked "draft, not picked", in place of options rounds first.

**Where.** `docs/design/prototype-v5/` (the board `Prototype v5.dc.html`, its scripts and styles, on DS v1's tokens and kit), kept in the repo outside the three Claude Design copies, like the explainer pages (MA-226): the claude-design connector writes only inline file contents, the prototype is about a megabyte, and standalone Claude Design closes on 14 Dec 2026 (MA-259). Its figure sets in `docs/design/figures/` (`make_prototype_v5.py` joins household-v4, forecaster-v4, future-plans-v4 and the new talk, wealth, engine, news-share and team-india sets, each asserted by its own make script); the record in `docs/design/reviews/MA-291/`. A walk-through record, not a board: each screen Arun picks from it goes into the boards through MA-279.

**Acceptance.**

* One journey, one clock and one figure set: every figure adds up across every step and door; every page draws from the ledger as of its step's time.
* The spine is the recommendation loop: prices and history feed the rules engine and the Forecaster, which give each holding a stance (ADD shown as Buy, HOLD, PAUSE, TRIM, REBALANCE, WATCH) with its pillars and confidence; every call is graded on the track record and calibration; agents propose a rule or model change on that evidence, which the admin approves behind the second check. The app never trades: a signal, never a buy or sell button.
* Chapters for every phase 0 to 20 (117 steps in 21 chapters).
* At every door, light and dark, privacy mode, both members' views; create in the chat, correct in place.
* Each screen not yet picked carries a "Draft, not picked" chip.
* Gates: plan-sync, design-sync, board-fit (walks every chapter and step at the five doors), the contrast gate, and the new prototype-v5 gate (`scripts/prototype_smoke.js`: every step at every door in light and dark and with privacy on; script errors, pages not drawn, pages wider than their door, wrong weekdays, tools ARCHITECTURE 8 does not define, em dashes, Telegram, money left showing). Published as a private Artifact for the walk-through.

issues.title: The design-sync gate fails on every project since Claude Design appends a closing notice to its results
issues.description_html:
**What happened.** On 30 Oct 2026, `python3 scripts/design_sync.py check` failed on all three projects: "cannot list MyPaisa app v1 (...): the listing of ... is not JSON". The standalone Claude Design server now appends a closing notice to every result, after the listing's JSON and after read_file's closing tag: "Notice: this MCP server belongs to standalone Claude Design (claude.ai/design). All its tools, the reading ones included, stop working no later than December 14, 2026, because Claude Design now lives in Claude. ...". The JSON no longer parses, and a file read would carry the notice into the copy, so `pull` would no longer be byte for byte. The gate and the PR hook block every PR in the repo until it is fixed.

**Where.** `scripts/design_sync.py` (`result_text`).

**Fix.** Cut the server's notice from every connector result (inline, saved to a file, or a saved list of text blocks) before anything reads it. Two selftest readings prove it: a listing with the notice parses to the listing, and a read with the notice after its tag gives the content alone; both fail with the fix reverted (checked on a copy).

**Acceptance.**

* `design_sync.py selftest`: 13 readings, 0 wrong; the two new cases fail when the fix is reverted.
* `design_sync.py check` lists all three projects again.
* Gates: plan-sync, design-sync.

**Found in.** MA-291 (its PR is blocked by this gate); fixed on its branch. Relates to MA-259 and MA-260 (the connector stops working by 14 Dec 2026).

issues.title: The board gate's diff crashes against any ref from before Prototype v5, so three of MA-240's ledger checks fail

MA-291 (merged in PR #68, 3691968) added `REPO_BOARDS` to `boards()` and made a listed repo-only board that is missing a failure, so that the gate fails closed on the current tree; but the diff mode also lists the boards of the base ref it compares against, and a ref from before 29 Oct has no Prototype v5.

**Where.** `scripts/board_fit.js`, `boards()` and the diff's base listing.

**Fix.** A repo-only board that is missing is a failure on the tree being checked, and is simply absent from a base ref (the diff then reports it as a new board, as it does for any board added since). Proved by the three MA-240 checks passing, and by a selftest-style run on a copy where the current tree lacks the prototype (still refused).

**Where.** `PRODUCT.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `.impeccable/design.json`, `.impeccable/config.json`, `docs/design/ds-v1/`, `docs/design/ios-v1/`, `docs/design/app-v1/`, `docs/design/prototype-v5/`, `docs/design/reviews/MA-295/build_boards.py`, `scripts/contrast_check.py`, `scripts/prototype_smoke.js`, `PLAN.md`, `docs/trace.json`, `docs/roadmap.json`, `docs/confluence/`

* Undefined `--mp-uk` and `--mp-in` chart tokens are fixed to canonical `--mp-chart-line` and `--mp-chart-2` across `Chart options.dc.html` at all three doors (`MA-295/build_boards.py`), rendering the picked `1a Monzo Pulse` UK wealth bar and `1c` country donut visibly in light and dark, and `--mp-ccy-inr` is added to `tokens.css` and `scripts/contrast_check.py`; `Foundations.dc.html`, `Components.dc.html`, `Components 2.dc.html` and `MyPaisa DS v1.dc.html` update stale read-only / sign-in prose while preserving `Kind icons.dc.html`'s `MA-241` pinned palette and leaving the 37 pre-`8e4b675` comparison boards untouched for `review/MA-240` ahead of `MA-278` and `MA-279`.
* Protruding 100%-plan benchmark ticks (`.has-tick` + `.mp-track-clip` / `.bar-clip`) clip their inner capsule fill without slicing off the vertical tick overhang; board-level `a:hover` rules on updated canvases and shared button `:hover` rules in `tokens.css` / `ios.css` protect `.mp-btn-primary` and `.cbtn` foreground contrast; `:focus-visible`, `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` (matching `.t-dark`), `@media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce)`, `@media (prefers-contrast: more)`, `< 900px` iPad `.insp` hiding, invisible 44x44 hit-area expansion on compact controls, and batched `motion.js` reads/writes land in `ds-v1` and sync byte-for-byte to `ios-v1` and `app-v1`, keeping every pre-`8e4b675` board pixel-identical at its drawn size (`review/MA-240`).
* Privacy Mode redacts raw `£`, `₹`, `$` and `€` figures at the formatter, DOM text, `aria-label` and interactive `[data-scrub]` tooltip layers across `Prototype v5`, the `Chart options` canvases and the post-`8e4b675` `Projection` / `Plans` / `Budget forecast` `v4` boards; `Web v4 · Projection.dc.html` and `iPhone v4 · Projection.dc.html` bind `Today's money` `aria-checked` to `tmA`; `[data-scrub]` handles `pointerup`, `pointercancel`, `focusout` and keyboard `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`/`Escape`.
* `Prototype v5` adds a 5th `More` drawer and `Search` on `<=1023px` Web so all routes (`Holdings`, `Overlap`, `Track record`, `News`, `Search`, `Reports`, `Admin center`, etc.) are reachable on mobile and tablet web; strips iOS Liquid Glass (`.lg`, `.lg-tint`, `.sheet-grab`) and fake iPhone bezel padding from `desk` and `pweb` Web frames (and `.w390` in `Chart options`); adds `aria-hidden="true"` to all decorative `.ms` icons; and makes every modal sheet (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`) dismissible via backdrop, close control and `Escape` (including steps without `sheetClose`).
* Gates: `scripts/contrast_check.py` verifies `--mp-ccy-inr`, checks `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` parity with `.t-dark`, and refuses undefined `var(--mp-*)`/`var(--lg-*)` tokens and unscoped `a:hover` colour rules (with `--selftest` cases); `scripts/prototype_smoke.js` refuses `.ms:not([aria-hidden="true"])`, `.lg` on Web doors, and raw currency amounts anywhere in DOM text, `aria-label` attributes or `[data-scrub]` payloads under `--priv` (with `--selftest` cases and interactive Playwright assertions); `plan-sync`, `contrast_check`, `prototype-v5` and `board-fit` gates pass green.
